# Slipstream UI — LLM Documentation Index

The AI-first React component library. 82 components, each shipping a
machine-readable COMPONENT_MANIFEST; this directory mirrors those manifests as markdown.

- Library docs: https://slipstreamui.com/docs
- Manifest registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/all.json
- Single-file corpus: https://slipstreamui.com/llms-full.txt
- shadcn-compatible install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://slipstreamui.com/registry/<id>.json`

## Core components (@slipstream-ui/core) — 65

- [Accordion](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/accordion.md) — Collapsible content sections with ARIA accordion semantics and keyboard navigation
- [Alert](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/alert.md) — Inline alert for status messages with semantic variants (destructive, success, warning, info)
- [AppShell](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/app-shell.md) — Application frame with a sectioned sidebar, sticky header and scrolling main; the sidebar becomes a left Drawer on small screens.
- [AuthLayout](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/auth-layout.md) — Centered authentication surface: brand, title/description, form card and footer, with size presets.
- [Autocomplete](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/autocomplete.md) — Free-text type-ahead input with a portalled listbox: static or async options, grouped headings, descriptions and custom rows.
- [Avatar](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/avatar.md) — A user profile image component with fallback support and accessible image loading
- [Badge](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/badge.md) — A small status indicator component for displaying tags, counts, or status information
- [Block](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/block.md) — Semantic container (div by default, swappable element) — the structural counterpart to Text (p).
- [Breadcrumb](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/breadcrumb.md) — Navigation breadcrumb trail with links and current-page indicator
- [Button](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/button.md) — A clickable button component with variants for different visual styles and sizes
- [ButtonGroup](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/button-group.md) — Joins buttons into one segmented control: adjacent borders collapse, middle corners square off, and only the outer corners stay rounded — a single outline around the group.
- [Card](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/card.md) — A content container with header, body, and footer sections for grouping related information
- [Checkbox](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/checkbox.md) — A native checkbox input styled to match the design system, plus CheckboxGroup for grouping related options under an accessible legend
- [ConfirmDialog](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/confirm-dialog.md) — Accessible confirmation dialog with async pending state, destructive variant and cancellable actions, built on Dialog.
- [DataTable](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/data-table.md) — Config-driven table: one component plus a columns config that owns shape, sorting, pagination, and row interaction.
- [DatePicker](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/date-picker.md) — Native date field with an ISO-string contract, min/max passthrough and an optional clear button.
- [Dialog](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/dialog.md) — Accessible modal dialog with focus trap/restore, backdrop and Escape dismissal, size presets, optional header/footer slots, a scrollable body, and opt-in fade motion.
- [Drawer](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/drawer.md) — Edge sheet for secondary flows: slides from any side (sm/md/lg), with Dialog-grade modal semantics (portal, focus trap, Escape, focus restoration).
- [EmptyState](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/empty-state.md) — Placeholder for empty collections, zero-result searches and unconfigured features, with title, description and action slots.
- [Fieldset](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/fieldset.md) — Groups related form controls in a native fieldset with a legend, optional description, and an error slot.
- [FileUpload](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/file-upload.md) — Drag-and-drop file picker with a removable file list and per-file progress bars.
- [FilterBar](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/filter-bar.md) — List-page filter strip: search field, filter controls, reset affordance and trailing actions.
- [Flex / FlexItem](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/flex.md) — Typed flexbox container (direction/align/justify/wrap/gap) with FlexItem for per-child grow/shrink/basis controls.
- [Form](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/form.md) — Semantic form element with even-spacing layouts: stacked (default), bordered card, or inline row — native submit and validation untouched.
- [FormField](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/form-field.md) — Label + control + hint/error in one unit with htmlFor, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid wiring applied automatically.
- [FormLayout](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/form-layout.md) — Groups form fields with even, tokenized spacing: vertical stack, horizontal row, or 1-4 column grid, optionally as a semantic fieldset.
- [Grid / GridItem](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/grid.md) — Typed CSS grid with column counts per breakpoint (literal utilities that survive purging), auto-fit min-column mode, and GridItem spans.
- [Heading](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/heading.md) — Semantic heading (h1-h6) with a safe default scale and an optional visual-size override.
- [Input](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/input.md) — A text input field with support for various input types and standard HTML input attributes
- [InputGroup](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/input-group.md) — Composite input shell with flush left/right addons (icons, units, buttons) behind one outer outline; the nested field sheds its own border so the group reads as a single control.
- [Label](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/label.md) — An accessible form label that associates with its control
- [Link](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/link.md) — Inline link primitive with default/muted/underline/arrow/external variants, asChild router support and safe external handling.
- [LinkTabs](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/link-tabs.md) — Route-driven navigation tabs that render real links and mark the current path with aria-current="page".
- [List / ListItem](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/list.md) — Semantic list (ul/li) for rows of related items: settings, results, nav — with leading/trailing slots, selection, and pressable rows.
- [Menu](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/menu.md) — Dropdown menu with keyboard navigation, typeahead, and ARIA menu semantics
- [MetricCard](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/metric-card.md) — KPI tile: label, value, directional delta (arrow + color) and supporting hint.
- [PageHeader](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/page-header.md) — Standard page heading: optional breadcrumbs, level-1 title, description, right-aligned actions and a sub-row slot.
- [Pagination](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/pagination.md) — Numeric pagination with prev/next and boundary jumps; accepts page/pageCount or currentPage/totalPages and derives the count (plus a Showing X-Y of Z summary) from total/pageSize.
- [PasswordInput](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/password-input.md) — Password field with an accessible show/hide toggle (aria-pressed), built on Input.
- [Popover](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/popover.md) — Floating panel anchored to a trigger with interactive content, closing on outside click and Escape
- [Progress](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/progress.md) — A determinate progress bar with role=progressbar and exact value semantics
- [Prose](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/prose.md) — Self-contained long-form typography for rendered markdown/MDX: headings, links, lists, code, tables, quotes and figures.
- [Radio](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/radio.md) — Native radio buttons grouped for mutually exclusive choices, with an accessible fieldset/legend wrapper
- [Search](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/search.md) — Select-with-search: type to filter a full-width dropdown of options, or arrow through the full set from an empty query.
- [SectionHeading](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/section-heading.md) — Section heading block: eyebrow, title (level 2-4), description and actions, with left/center alignment and three sizes.
- [Select](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/select.md) — Accessible select built on the native <select> with flat options, optgroups, a placeholder row and native multi-select.
- [SelectMenu](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/select-menu.md) — Custom listbox select for rich options: descriptions, icons, groups, multi-select, custom rows and hidden inputs for forms.
- [Separator](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/separator.md) — A visual divider between content blocks, decorative or semantic
- [SiteFooter](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/site-footer.md) — Marketing footer: brand + tagline column, link columns and a legal bar; router-agnostic via linkComponent.
- [SiteHeader](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/site-header.md) — Marketing/site header: sticky bar with brand, horizontal navigation with prefix-aware active states, right-aligned actions and a mobile drawer.
- [Skeleton](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/skeleton.md) — A loading placeholder that mirrors the shape of upcoming content
- [Spinner](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/spinner.md) — Indeterminate loading indicator with accessible status semantics.
- [Stepper](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/stepper.md) — Multi-step flow indicator: ordered list, aria-current step, text state for complete/current/upcoming.
- [Switch](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/switch.md) — A toggle switch for binary settings, with role=switch and aria-checked
- [Table](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/table.md) — Semantic data table with headers, body, footer, and accessible caption
- [TableCard](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/table-card.md) — Table shell with title/description, header actions, optional toolbar, edge-to-edge body and a footer row.
- [TableOfContents](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/table-of-contents.md) — Sticky 'On this page' navigation with nested levels and aria-current, plus a useScrollSpy hook for the active heading.
- [Tabs](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/tabs.md) — Tabbed content container with ARIA tablist semantics and keyboard navigation
- [Text](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/text.md) — Semantic paragraph text with a controlled type scale; renders a real p (or span with inline).
- [Textarea](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/textarea.md) — A multi-line text input styled to match Input, wrapping the native textarea
- [ThemeToggle](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/theme-toggle.md) — Presentational light/dark toggle with accessible labels and sun/moon state.
- [TimePicker](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/time-picker.md) — Native time field with an HH:MM contract and an optional clear button.
- [Timeline](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/timeline.md) — Vertical chronology for experience, activity and audit trails, built on an ordered list.
- [Toast](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/toast.md) — Accessible notifications: tree-scoped provider/hook plus an imperative toast() API rendered by <Toaster />.
- [Tooltip](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/tooltip.md) — Hover/focus tooltip with aria-describedby association, delay, and Escape dismissal

## AI components (@slipstream-ui/ai) — 17

- [Attachment / AttachmentList](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/attachment.md) — File chips for prompts and messages. `Attachment` renders one file; `AttachmentList` renders a wrapping row. Display-only: upload and file-system logic stay in the consumer.
- [Branch](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/branch.md) — Variant navigation for branched messages: previous/next arrows with an N/M position indicator.
- [ChainThought](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/chain-thought.md) — Displays ordered reasoning steps with status indicators.
- [CodeBlock](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/code-block.md) — Syntax-highlighted code block with language label and copy-to-clipboard button.
- [CommandPalette](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/command-palette.md) — Cmd+K style command palette with lexical search, sectioned results and full keyboard navigation
- [Confirmation](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/confirmation.md) — Human-in-the-loop approval gate for agent actions. Pauses execution until the user approves or rejects.
- [Conversation](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/conversation.md) — A container for displaying a list of chat messages with auto-scroll and loading states
- [InlineCitation](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/inline-citation.md) — Perplexity-style inline citation chip that reveals the source title and snippet on hover or keyboard focus.
- [Message](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/message.md) — A chat message component that displays messages from users, assistants, or system prompts with optional avatars
- [MessageActions](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/message-actions.md) — Feedback toolbar for an AI response: copy to clipboard, thumbs up/down rating, and regenerate. Every action is a callback; the component holds no conversation state.
- [PromptInput](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/prompt-input.md) — A textarea input for entering chat prompts with auto-resize, keyboard shortcuts, and send button
- [Reasoning](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/reasoning.md) — A collapsible component for displaying AI reasoning steps and chain-of-thought processes
- [Response](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/response.md) — Streaming-optimized markdown renderer for AI responses with GFM support, streaming-safe repair of incomplete syntax, and highlighted code blocks with copy.
- [Source / Sources](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/source.md) — Displays citations and references for an AI response. `Source` renders a single citation; `Sources` renders a numbered list with an overflow count.
- [StreamingIndicator](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/streaming-indicator.md) — Shows that an AI response is currently streaming.
- [Suggestions](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/suggestions.md) — Displays clickable follow-up prompts for AI interactions.
- [ToolCall](https://slipstreamui.com/llm/components/tool-call.md) — A component for displaying AI tool/function calls with status, arguments, and results

## Usage guidance

1. Read the component .md page before generating code — it lists exact prop names,
   required props, anti-patterns, and accessibility requirements.
2. Never invent props not present in the Props table.
3. Components are stateless and uncontrolled unless documented otherwise;
   consumers own conversation/thread state.

# Accordion

Collapsible content sections with ARIA accordion semantics and keyboard navigation

> Import: `import { Accordion } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/accordion.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Accordion organizes content into expandable sections, reducing visual density on pages with lots of content. Each trigger announces its expanded state and controls its panel.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| value | `string[]` | — | no | Controlled open item ids |
| defaultValue | `string[]` | — | no | Initial open item ids when uncontrolled |
| onValueChange | `(value: string[]) => void` | — | no | Called when the open set changes |
| collapsible | `boolean` | `true` | no | When true, opening an item closes the others |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | yes | AccordionItem children |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |
| icon | `ReactNode` | — | no | AccordionTrigger only: replace the default chevron rendered at the far right of the header. |
| variant | `'default' | 'borderless'` | `default` | no | 'default' = bordered card with dividers; 'borderless' = plain stacked sections. |
| gap | `'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | number` | — | no | Token gap ('lg') or exact pixels (16) between items. |

## Examples

### FAQ accordion

Single-open accordion for FAQs

```tsx
<Accordion defaultValue={['a']}>
  <AccordionItem id="a">
    <AccordionTrigger>What is Slipstream?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>An AI-first component system.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem id="b">
    <AccordionTrigger>How do I install?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Run npx slipstream-ui init.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Accordion for primary navigation** — Accordion is for content disclosure. Use Tabs or a nav menu for page-level navigation.
- **Don't hide required information behind a collapsed panel** — Users may not discover it. Put critical content in the open by default.

## Accessibility

- **Accordion semantics**: Trigger has aria-expanded and aria-controls; panel has role=region and aria-labelledby
- **Keyboard support**: Enter/Space toggle; hidden panels are removed from tab order

## Composition

- Compose with **AccordionItem** — Wrap each section in an AccordionItem with a unique id
  
  ```tsx
  <AccordionItem id="x"><AccordionTrigger>...</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>...</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
  ```
- Related: Tabs, Card

---

# Alert

Inline alert for status messages with semantic variants (destructive, success, warning, info)

> Import: `import { Alert } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/alert.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Alert communicates status or requires attention. Use it for form errors, success confirmations, warnings, and informational notices. Renders role=alert so screen readers announce it immediately.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| variant | `'default' | 'destructive' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'info'` | `'default'` | no | Semantic style variant |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | yes | Alert content (AlertTitle and AlertDescription) |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Examples

### Destructive alert

Error state with title and description

```tsx
<Alert variant="destructive">
  <AlertTitle>Error</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>Your session has expired. Please log in again.</AlertDescription>
</Alert>
```

### Success alert

Confirmation of a completed action

```tsx
<Alert variant="success">
  <AlertTitle>Success</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>Your changes have been saved.</AlertDescription>
</Alert>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Alert for transient notifications** — Alert is persistent inline content. Use Toast for temporary notifications that auto-dismiss.
- **Don't use Alert for required form validation** — Field-level errors belong next to the field with aria-describedby. Use Alert only for form-level errors.

## Accessibility

- **Live region**: role=alert announces the content when it appears
- **Heading semantics**: AlertTitle renders as h5

## Composition

- Compose with **AlertTitle + AlertDescription** — Pair title with description for structured alerts
  
  ```tsx
  <Alert><AlertTitle>Title</AlertTitle><AlertDescription>Body</AlertDescription></Alert>
  ```
- Related: Toast, Badge

---

# AppShell

Application frame with a sectioned sidebar, sticky header and scrolling main; the sidebar becomes a left Drawer on small screens.

> Import: `import { AppShell } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/app-shell.json
> Tier: organism · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Every dashboard hand-rolls the same shell: rail, header, scroll owner, and a mobile nav. AppShell owns the structure and responsive switch while staying presentational — you pass the active route and a router link component, so it works with React Router, Next Link, or plain anchors.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sidebar | `ReactNode` | — | no | Desktop rail content; also rendered inside the mobile drawer (AppShell). |
| header | `ReactNode` | — | no | Sticky top bar content (AppShell). |
| hideMobileMenu | `boolean` | `false` | no | Hide the built-in burger button when the header owns navigation (AppShell). |
| sidebarWidth | `string` | `w-64` | no | Tailwind width class for the desktop rail (AppShell). |
| sections | `{ title?: string; items: SidebarItem[] }[]` | — | yes | Grouped navigation items (Sidebar). |
| heading | `ReactNode` | — | no | Brand/mark at the top of the rail (Sidebar). |
| footer | `ReactNode` | — | no | Bottom area of the rail (Sidebar). |
| activeHref | `string` | — | no | Current route; matching items get aria-current=page (Sidebar). |
| linkComponent | `React.ElementType` | `a` | no | Router link component (react-router Link, Next Link) (Sidebar). |
| label | `string` | `Primary` | no | Accessible name of the nav landmark (Sidebar). |
| children | `SidebarItem[]` | — | no | Nested items — renders a collapsible group with aria-expanded (SidebarItem). |
| collapsible | `boolean` | `false` | no | Shows the collapse/expand control (Sidebar). |
| defaultCollapsed | `boolean` | `false` | no | Initial collapsed state (Sidebar). |
| collapsed | `boolean` | — | no | Controlled collapsed state (Sidebar). |
| onCollapsedChange | `(collapsed: boolean) => void` | — | no | Fires when the rail collapses/expands (Sidebar). |
| defaultExpanded | `string[]` | — | no | SidebarItem hrefs of groups open initially (Sidebar). |
| mobileBreakpoint | `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` | `md` | no | Breakpoint where the rail becomes a drawer (AppShell). |

## Examples

### Dashboard shell

Router-agnostic: pass your Link component and the current path.

```tsx
import { AppShell, Sidebar } from '@slipstream-ui/core';

<AppShell
  header={<h1 className="text-sm font-semibold">Studio</h1>}
  sidebar={
    <Sidebar
      activeHref={pathname}
      linkComponent={RouterLink}
      heading={<strong>Acme</strong>}
      sections={[
        { title: 'Workspace', items: [{ href: '/dashboard', label: 'Dashboard' }, { href: '/classes', label: 'Classes', badge: 4 }] },
      ]}
    />
  }
>
  <Page />
</AppShell>
```

### Header only

Skip the sidebar when the product is a single surface.

```tsx
<AppShell header={<TopBar />}>
  <Page />
</AppShell>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't nest scroll containers** — AppShell's main is the scroll owner. Adding h-screen/overflow-hidden wrappers inside breaks sticky headers and mobile drawer focus.
- **Don't hardcode anchors for SPA routes** — Plain <a href> triggers full page loads in client-side routers. Pass your router's Link via linkComponent.

## Accessibility

- **Nav landmark**: Sidebar renders nav with an accessible name (label prop)
- **Current route**: aria-current=page on the active item
- **Mobile drawer**: The rail becomes a Drawer with focus trap, Escape, focus restore and a labelled dialog

## Composition

- Compose with **Drawer** — AppShell mounts the mobile navigation Drawer for you when a sidebar is provided
  
  ```tsx
  <AppShell sidebar={<Sidebar sections={sections} />}>…</AppShell>
  ```
- Compose with **Button** — Header actions live in the header slot
  
  ```tsx
  <AppShell header={<Button>New</Button>}>…</AppShell>
  ```
- Related: Drawer, Button, Breadcrumb, Menu

---

# Attachment / AttachmentList

File chips for prompts and messages. `Attachment` renders one file; `AttachmentList` renders a wrapping row. Display-only: upload and file-system logic stay in the consumer.

> Import: `import { Attachment } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/attachment.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

Show what files are part of a conversation turn (name, size, type, thumbnail, upload status) without coupling the library to any upload implementation.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| attachment | `AttachmentItem` | — | yes | File descriptor: id, name, size, type, previewUrl, status. |
| attachments | `AttachmentItem[]` | — | yes | Files to display (AttachmentList). |
| onRemove | `(attachment) => void` | — | no | Remove callback; omit to hide remove controls. |

## Examples

### Prompt attachments

```tsx
<AttachmentList attachments={[{ id: '1', name: 'spec.pdf', size: '2.4 MB', status: 'done' }]} onRemove={remove} />
```

### Uploading image

```tsx
<Attachment attachment={{ id: '2', name: 'chart.png', previewUrl: '/chart.png', status: 'uploading' }} />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not use Attachment for drag-and-drop targets** — The chip displays an existing item; build dropzones in the consumer and render AttachmentList once items exist.

## Accessibility

- **Remove control**: Icon-only remove button has an aria-label including the file name.
- **Upload status**: Uploading state is announced via role=status.
- **Decorative thumbnails**: Preview images are aria-hidden; the file name carries the meaning.

---

# AuthLayout

Centered authentication surface: brand, title/description, form card and footer, with size presets.

> Import: `import { AuthLayout } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/auth-layout.json
> Tier: organism · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Sign-in, sign-up, reset and verify screens should look identical. AuthLayout owns the centered card, brand slot and footer so auth pages only supply the form.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| title | `string` | — | yes | Card heading (h1). |
| description | `string` | — | no | Supporting line under the heading. |
| brand | `ReactNode` | — | no | Mark rendered above the card. |
| footer | `ReactNode` | — | no | Links/legal copy under the card. |
| size | `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` | `md` | no | Card width preset. |

## Examples

### Sign in

Form lives inside the card.

```tsx
<AuthLayout
  title="Sign in"
  description="Welcome back."
  brand={<Logo />}
  footer={<a href="/signup">Create account</a>}
>
  <SignInForm />
</AuthLayout>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't nest another full-height page** — AuthLayout already owns min-h-screen centering.

## Accessibility

- **One h1**: Renders the page heading

## Composition

- Compose with **Form** — Place the Form inside children
  
  ```tsx
  <AuthLayout title="Sign in"><Form onSubmit={…}>…</Form></AuthLayout>
  ```
- Related: Form, PasswordInput, Button

---

# Autocomplete

Free-text type-ahead input with a portalled listbox: static or async options, grouped headings, descriptions and custom rows.

> Import: `import { Autocomplete } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/autocomplete.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Free text stays first-class: any value may be typed, while matching options accelerate entry. Async sources are debounced with stale-response guards; grouped headings and custom rows cover searchable-select patterns; Escape/arrow keys follow the combobox model.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| suggestions | `string[]` | — | no | Deprecated — use options. |
| value | `string` | — | no | Current text — standard controlled-input contract (wire onValueChange to update it). |
| defaultValue | `string` | `''` | no | Initial text when uncontrolled. |
| onValueChange | `(value: string) => void` | — | no | Fires on every keystroke AND on suggestion selection (like a native input's onChange). |
| emptyText | `string` | — | no | Shown when no option matches. |
| options | `Array<string | AutocompleteOption>` | — | no | Static options; strings or { value, label?, group?, description? }. |
| loadOptions | `(query: string) => Promise<Array<string | AutocompleteOption>>` | — | no | Async option source; debounced and guarded against stale responses. |
| renderOption | `(option, state: { active: boolean }) => ReactNode` | — | no | Custom row renderer. |
| clearable | `boolean` | `false` | no | Shows a clear button once the field has text. |
| loadingText | `string` | — | no | Shown while async options load. |
| debounceMs | `number` | `200` | no | Debounce for loadOptions in ms. |

## Examples

### Async search

Debounced async source with stale-response guard and clear.

```tsx
<Autocomplete
  aria-label="Search people"
  clearable
  loadOptions={async (query) => searchPeople(query)}
/>
```

### Grouped options with descriptions

Section headings plus a supporting line per row.

```tsx
<Autocomplete
  aria-label="Search"
  options={[
    { value: 'ada', label: 'Ada Lovelace', group: 'People', description: 'Mathematician' },
    { value: 'rust', label: 'Rust', group: 'Languages' },
  ]}
/>
```

### Controlled form field

onValueChange mirrors native onChange; FormField wires the label and hint.

```tsx
const [framework, setFramework] = useState('');

<FormField id="framework" label="Primary framework" hint="Type or pick a suggestion">
  <Autocomplete
    suggestions={['react', 'remix', 'next', 'vite']}
    value={framework}
    onValueChange={setFramework}
    name="framework"
    autoComplete="off"
  />
</FormField>
```

### Native autofill hints alongside the custom list

The native autoComplete attribute passes through — browser autofill and the suggestion list coexist.

```tsx
<Autocomplete
  name="country"
  autoComplete="country-name"
  suggestions={countryNames}
  onValueChange={setCountry}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Autocomplete for constrained choice** — Free text is the point of Autocomplete. When only known values are valid (plan tier, enum), use Select or Search so invalid states cannot be typed.
- **Don't forget to keep state in sync when controlled** — With value set, React makes the input fully controlled — if onValueChange does not update the parent state, typing appears frozen.
- **Don't block Enter for form submission** — Enter only consumes the event when a suggestion is actively highlighted — otherwise it should submit the surrounding form. Avoid adding a global keydown handler that always prevents Enter.

## Accessibility

- **Combobox pattern**: role=combobox with aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-autocomplete=list, and aria-activedescendant on the input; suggestions render as role=option with aria-selected
- **Keyboard operation**: ArrowDown/ArrowUp highlight suggestions (wrapping), Home/End jump, Enter accepts the highlighted suggestion, Escape closes the list; unhighlighted Enter submits the form natively
- **Native autocomplete passthrough**: The autoComplete attribute is forwarded to the input so browser autofill hints keep working

## Composition

- Compose with **FormField** — Standard form placement — label, hint, and error wiring come free
  
  ```tsx
  <FormField id="tag" label="Tag" hint="Type to see existing tags"><Autocomplete suggestions={tags} value={tag} onValueChange={setTag} /></FormField>
  ```
- Compose with **Search** — Search when values MUST come from the list; Autocomplete when free text stays valid
- Related: Search, Input, FormField, Select

---

# Avatar

A user profile image component with fallback support and accessible image loading

> Import: `import { Avatar } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/avatar.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

The Avatar component displays user profile images with a circular frame. It includes fallback content when the image fails to load or is not provided, and follows accessibility best practices for user avatars.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| src | `string` | — | no | URL of the avatar image |
| alt | `string` | — | no | Alt text for the avatar image (for accessibility) |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply to the avatar container |

## Examples

### Avatar with image

Avatar with image and fallback text

```tsx
<Avatar>
  <AvatarImage src="/avatar.jpg" alt="User" />
  <AvatarFallback>JD</AvatarFallback>
</Avatar>
```

### Avatar with fallback only

Avatar showing only fallback initials

```tsx
<Avatar>
  <AvatarFallback>JD</AvatarFallback>
</Avatar>
```

### Large avatar

Avatar with custom size

```tsx
<Avatar className="h-16 w-16">
  <AvatarImage src="/avatar.jpg" alt="User" />
  <AvatarFallback>JD</AvatarFallback>
</Avatar>
```

### Avatar with colored fallback

Avatar with styled fallback background

```tsx
<Avatar>
  <AvatarImage src="/avatar.jpg" alt="User" />
  <AvatarFallback className="bg-primary text-primary-foreground">JD</AvatarFallback>
</Avatar>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't forget alt text** — Alt text is essential for accessibility. Always describe the avatar content.
- **Don't use vague fallback text** — Fallback should be meaningful. Use initials or abbreviations that identify the user.
- **Don't use avatars for non-people** — Avatars are designed for people. Use other components for logos or objects.

## Accessibility

- **Screen reader support**: AvatarImage requires alt text. AvatarFallback content is announced when image fails
- **Image loading**: Radix Avatar handles image loading errors and displays fallback automatically
- **Focus indication**: Avatar can be focused and has visible focus ring when keyboard navigable

## Composition

- Compose with **Message** — Avatars are commonly used in Message components to identify the sender
  
  ```tsx
  Message component uses Avatar to show user or assistant identity
  ```
- Compose with **UserMenu** — Avatars are often used in user menus or profile headers
  
  ```tsx
  UserMenu displays current user's avatar for quick identification
  ```
- Related: Message, UserMenu, Button

---

# Badge

A small status indicator component for displaying tags, counts, or status information

> Import: `import { Badge } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/badge.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

The Badge component is used to display small pieces of information like status indicators, counts, or tags. It provides visual variants for different semantic meanings (default, secondary, destructive, outline).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| variant | `'default' | 'secondary' | 'destructive' | 'outline' | 'primary' | 'danger' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'info'` | `default` | no | Semantic surface; primary/danger are aliases for default/destructive. |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content to display inside the badge |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |
| asChild | `boolean` | `false` | no | Render the child element with badge styling. |

## Examples

### Tag linking to a filter

Tag that navigates.

```tsx
<Badge asChild>
  <Link href="/tags/react">React</Link>
</Badge>
```

### Default badge

Primary badge for highlighting new items

```tsx
<Badge>New</Badge>
```

### Secondary badge

Less prominent badge for secondary information

```tsx
<Badge variant="secondary">Info</Badge>
```

### Destructive badge

Badge for error states or destructive actions

```tsx
<Badge variant="destructive">Error</Badge>
```

### Outline badge

Subtle badge with outline style

```tsx
<Badge variant="outline">Beta</Badge>
```

### Count badge

Badge for displaying counts or numbers

```tsx
<Badge>3</Badge>
```

### Status badge

Badge for status indicators

```tsx
<Badge variant="outline">Active</Badge>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use for long text** — Badges are designed for short text. Use tooltips or other components for longer content.
- **Don't overuse badges** — Too many badges create visual noise. Prioritize the most important information.
- **Don't use wrong variant for meaning** — Destructive variant should only be used for errors or destructive actions.

## Accessibility

- **Screen reader support**: Badge content is announced as text. Use aria-label if badge has visual-only meaning
- **Color contrast**: All variants meet WCAG AA contrast requirements
- **Focus indication**: Badge has visible focus ring when keyboard navigable

## Composition

- Compose with **Button** — Badges can be combined with buttons to show notification counts or status
  
  ```tsx
  <Button><Badge>3</Badge> Messages</Button>
  ```
- Compose with **Card** — Badges are often used in card headers to show status or category
  
  ```tsx
  <Card><CardHeader><Badge>New</Badge></CardHeader></Card>
  ```
- Related: Button, Card, Tooltip

# Block

Semantic container (div by default, swappable element) — the structural counterpart to Text (p).

> Import: `import { Block } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/block.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Layout wrappers should still mean something: section, article, figure. Block is a typed, discoverable div that picks the element matching the content's role, with an inline (span) variation for flow contexts — no default decoration, so it composes with any utilities.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| as | `'div' | 'span' | 'section' | 'article' | 'figure' | 'header' | 'footer' | 'nav' | 'main' | 'aside'` | `div` | no | Semantic element to render. |
| inline | `boolean` | `false` | no | Shorthand for as="span" — inline flow instead of a block box. |
| muted | `boolean` | `false` | no | Use the muted-foreground token for the block's text. |

## Examples

### Semantic containers

```tsx
<Block as="section" className="space-y-2">
  <Heading level={3}>Related</Heading>
  <Text size="sm" muted>Prose lives in Text, not Block.</Text>
</Block>

<Block as="figure">…</Block>

{/* Inline flow */}
<Block inline>…</Block>
```

### Card-like surface via utilities

```tsx
<Block className="rounded-lg border border-border p-4">…</Block>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't put paragraphs inside Block** — Copy belongs in Text (p). Block is structure — mixing them loses document semantics.
- **Don't default to div when a landmark fits** — If the content is a section of page structure, as="section"/"article" gives assistive tech navigable landmarks for free.

## Accessibility

- **Element choice is explicit**: as/inline map to real intrinsic elements (semantic by selection)
- **No interactive defaults**: Block renders no focusable content of its own

## Composition

- Compose with **Text / Heading** — Block wraps structure; Text and Heading provide the content semantics
- Compose with **Flex / Grid** — Compose layout as Block → Flex/Grid → Text/Heading hierarchies
- Related: Text, Heading, Flex, Grid

---

# Branch

Variant navigation for branched messages: previous/next arrows with an N/M position indicator.

> Import: `import { Branch } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/branch.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

Let users compare alternative AI responses without leaving the transcript flow.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| count | `number` | — | yes | Total variants; renders nothing below 2. |
| selected | `number` | — | no | Controlled zero-based index. |
| defaultSelected | `number` | `0` | no | Uncontrolled initial index. |
| onSelect | `(index: number) => void` | — | no | Called with the chosen variant index. |
| labels | `object` | — | no | Overrides for previous/next aria-labels. |

## Examples

### Two variants

```tsx
<Branch count={variants.length} selected={i} onSelect={setI} />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not swap message content without syncing selected** — In controlled mode the displayed variant must follow onSelect.

## Accessibility

- **Boundary disabling**: Arrows disable at ends instead of wrapping silently.
- **Position announcement**: N/M indicator uses aria-live=polite.

# Breadcrumb

Navigation breadcrumb trail with links and current-page indicator

> Import: `import { Breadcrumb } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/breadcrumb.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Breadcrumb shows the user's location in a hierarchy and lets them navigate back to parent levels. The last item is the current page, marked with aria-current=page.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| items | `BreadcrumbItem[]` | — | yes | Ordered breadcrumb items; the last is the current page |
| separator | `ReactNode` | `'/'` | no | Separator character between items |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |
| onItemClick | `(item: BreadcrumbItem, index: number) => void` | — | no | Receives every link click with default navigation prevented — route programmatically. |
| linkComponent | `React.ElementType` | — | no | Custom link element for routers (preserves prefetch/modified clicks). |

## Examples

### Three-level breadcrumb

Hierarchical navigation with current page

```tsx
<Breadcrumb items={[
  { label: 'Home', href: '/' },
  { label: 'Docs', href: '/docs' },
  { label: 'Components' },
]} />
```

### Custom separator

Breadcrumb with a chevron separator

```tsx
<Breadcrumb
  items={[{ label: 'Home', href: '/' }, { label: 'Page' }]}
  separator="›"
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Breadcrumb for flat navigation** — Breadcrumb is for hierarchical structures. Use a nav menu or tabs for flat peer pages.
- **Don't make the current page a link** — The last item should be plain text with aria-current=page, not a link to itself.

## Accessibility

- **Navigation landmark**: nav[aria-label=Breadcrumb] so screen readers announce the landmark
- **Current page**: Last item has aria-current=page

## Composition

- Compose with **Link** — Non-last items should be links
  
  ```tsx
  <Breadcrumb items={[{ label: 'Home', href: '/' }, { label: 'Current' }]} />
  ```
- Related: Menu, Tabs

---

# Button

A clickable button component with variants for different visual styles and sizes

> Import: `import { Button } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/button.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

The Button component is a fundamental interactive element that triggers actions or navigation. It provides visual feedback through hover/active states and supports multiple variants to match different semantic contexts (primary actions, destructive actions, navigation, etc.).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| variant | `'default' | 'destructive' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'info' | 'outline' | 'outline-destructive' | 'outline-success' | 'outline-warning' | 'outline-info' | 'secondary' | 'ghost' | 'link'` | `default` | no | Visual style variant of the button |
| size | `'default' | 'sm' | 'lg' | 'icon'` | `default` | no | Size variant of the button |
| asChild | `boolean` | `false` | no | When true, renders as a child component using Radix Slot for composition |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disables the button and prevents interaction |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | no | Content to display inside the button |
| onClick | `(event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void` | — | no | Handler called when button is clicked |
| type | `'button' | 'submit' | 'reset'` | `button` | no | HTML button type attribute |
| loading | `boolean` | `false` | no | Shows a spinner, disables the button and sets aria-busy. |
| loadingLabel | `string` | `'Loading'` | no | Screen-reader text while loading; localize this for non-English apps. |

## Examples

### Primary action button

Default variant for primary actions in the interface

```tsx
<Button>Click me</Button>
```

### Destructive action

Use for destructive or dangerous actions like delete, remove, etc.

```tsx
<Button variant="destructive">Delete</Button>
```

### Outline button

Secondary action with less visual weight

```tsx
<Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
```

### Small button

Compact size for dense interfaces

```tsx
<Button size="sm">Small</Button>
```

### Icon button

Square button for icon-only actions

```tsx
<Button size="icon"><Icon /></Button>
```

### As link

Button styled as a link, using asChild for composition

```tsx
<Button variant="link" asChild><a href="/docs">Learn more</a></Button>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use for navigation alone** — Buttons should trigger actions, not just navigate. Use proper navigation components.
- **Don't nest buttons** — Never nest buttons - it breaks accessibility and HTML validity
- **Don't use vague text** — Button text should clearly describe what will happen

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard navigation**: Button is natively focusable and can be activated with Enter or Space key
- **Screen reader support**: Button role is automatically announced. Content is read as button label
- **Disabled state**: Disabled buttons are not focusable and screen readers announce as disabled

## Composition

- Compose with **Icon** — Buttons can contain icons alongside text or as icon-only buttons
  
  ```tsx
  <Button><Icon />Text</Button> or <Button size="icon"><Icon /></Button>
  ```
- Compose with **Dialog** — Buttons commonly trigger dialog open/close actions
  
  ```tsx
  <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Open dialog</Button>
  ```
- Related: IconButton, Link, Tooltip

---

# ButtonGroup

Joins buttons into one segmented control: adjacent borders collapse, middle corners square off, and only the outer corners stay rounded — a single outline around the group.

> Import: `import { ButtonGroup } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/button-group.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Related actions (view modes, zoom, toolbar steps) should read as one instrument, not scattered pills. ButtonGroup collapses adjacent borders with negative spacing so the joined outline matches InputGroup's single-border language, while focus rings lift above siblings instead of being clipped.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| orientation | `'horizontal' | 'vertical'` | `horizontal` | no | Stacked segments share vertical edges; default lays them side by side. |

## Examples

### View mode toggle

Three segments share one outline; aria-label names the group.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup aria-label="View mode">
  <Button variant="outline">List</Button>
  <Button variant="outline">Board</Button>
  <Button variant="outline">Calendar</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Vertical toolbar steps

Stacked segments share horizontal edges.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Step navigation">
  <Button variant="secondary">Step back</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">Step forward</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Stepper with primary action

Mix variants freely as long as each button keeps a border.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Pagination steps">
  <Button variant="outline">Previous</Button>
  <Button>Next</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use borderless variants inside** — Ghost/link buttons carry no border, so the joined outline breaks at that segment. The group's single-outline promise depends on every segment contributing an edge.
- **Don't group unrelated actions** — A joined outline asserts the segments are alternatives of one control. unrelated actions should stay separate Buttons so their relationship isn't overstated.

## Accessibility

- **Group semantics**: Renders role=group; pass aria-label (or aria-labelledby) so the group name is announced before its buttons
- **Focus visibility**: Focused segments get position:relative + z-10 so the ring paints above neighbours instead of clipping
- **Keyboard order**: Buttons keep native tab order; groups are not roving-tabindex widgets (use Tabs for that pattern)

## Composition

- Compose with **Button** — Direct children — each keeps its own variant/size but must keep a border
  
  ```tsx
  <ButtonGroup><Button variant="outline">One</Button><Button variant="outline">Two</Button></ButtonGroup>
  ```
- Compose with **Tabs** — For exclusive views with panels, use Tabs; ButtonGroup is for actions/tools, not view switching with content
  
  ```tsx
  <Tabs>…</Tabs>
  ```
- Related: Button, Tabs, Toolbar

---

# Card

A content container with header, body, and footer sections for grouping related information

> Import: `import { Card } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/card.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Card groups related content into a scannable container. Use it for settings panels, feature highlights, user profiles, and any content that benefits from visual grouping.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| children | `ReactNode` | — | yes | Card sub-components (CardHeader, CardContent, CardFooter) |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |
| asChild | `boolean` | `false` | no | Render the child element (router Link, <a>) with card styling instead of a div. |

## Examples

### Card as a link

Whole card becomes a semantic link without losing styling.

```tsx
<Card asChild>
  <Link href="/writing/hello">
    <CardHeader><CardTitle>Hello</CardTitle></CardHeader>
  </Link>
</Card>
```

### Basic card

Card with header, content, and footer

```tsx
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Profile</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Manage your account settings</CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>Form fields here</CardContent>
  <CardFooter>
    <Button>Save</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>
```

### Simple card

Minimal card without header or footer

```tsx
<Card>
  <CardContent>
    <p>Just a content block with a border.</p>
  </CardContent>
</Card>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't nest Cards** — Nesting cards creates visual noise. Use dividers or spacing within a single Card.

## Accessibility

- **Heading hierarchy**: CardTitle renders as h3

## Composition

- Compose with **Button** — Place primary actions in CardFooter
  
  ```tsx
  <CardFooter><Button>Save</Button></CardFooter>
  ```
- Related: Separator, Tabs

# Checkbox

A native checkbox input styled to match the design system, plus CheckboxGroup for grouping related options under an accessible legend

> Import: `import { Checkbox } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/checkbox.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

The Checkbox component is the standard way to let users select zero or more options from a set. It wraps the native input so keyboard, form, and screen-reader behavior is identical to platform checkboxes. CheckboxGroup is the multi-select counterpart of RadioGroup: shared name, fieldset/legend context, and the selection as a string[].

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| checked | `boolean` | — | no | Controlled checked state; omit for uncontrolled usage |
| defaultChecked | `boolean` | — | no | Initial checked state when uncontrolled |
| onCheckedChange | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — | no | Fired when the user toggles the checkbox |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disables the checkbox |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |
| legend | `string` | — | no | Accessible group label; rendered as <legend> inside a fieldset (CheckboxGroup component) |
| onValueChange | `(value: string[]) => void` | — | no | Called with the full selection after a toggle (CheckboxGroup component) |
| orientation | `'vertical' | 'horizontal'` | `vertical` | no | Stack options (default) or lay them out in a wrapping row (CheckboxGroup component) |
| error | `string` | — | no | Group-level validation message; announced via role=alert (CheckboxGroup component) |

## Examples

### Basic checkbox

Simple checkbox with an accessible label

```tsx
<Checkbox aria-label="Accept terms" />
```

### With visible label

Checkbox paired with a visible Label

```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-2">
  <Checkbox id="terms" />
  <Label htmlFor="terms">Accept terms</Label>
</div>
```

### Controlled checkbox

Checkbox driven by parent state

```tsx
<Checkbox
  checked={agreed}
  onCheckedChange={setAgreed}
  aria-label="Accept terms"
/>
```

### Multi-select group

Shared name, legend context, selection as string[]

```tsx
<CheckboxGroup
  name="langs"
  legend="Languages"
  defaultValue={["ts"]}
  onValueChange={setLangs}
>
  <CheckboxGroupItem value="ts" label="TypeScript" />
  <CheckboxGroupItem value="go" label="Go" />
</CheckboxGroup>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Checkbox for mutually exclusive choices** — Checkbox is for multi-select. Use Radio (inside RadioGroup) when only one option can be chosen.
- **Don't use Checkbox as a toggle for settings** — For binary settings that apply immediately, use Switch which announces on/off state.

## Accessibility

- **Native semantics**: Wraps input[type=checkbox]; keyboard and screen-reader behavior is the platform default
- **Focus indicator**: Visible ring on focus-visible

## Composition

- Compose with **Label** — Always pair with a Label or aria-label for accessibility
  
  ```tsx
  <Checkbox id="x" /><Label htmlFor="x">Accept</Label>
  ```
- Compose with **CheckboxGroup** — Wrap related checkboxes so they share a name and an announced group label
  
  ```tsx
  <CheckboxGroup name="x" legend="Options"><CheckboxGroupItem value="a" label="A" /></CheckboxGroup>
  ```
- Related: Radio, Switch, Label

---

# CodeBlock

Syntax-highlighted code block with language label and copy-to-clipboard button.

> Import: `import { CodeBlock } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/code-block.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

Display AI-generated or referenced code readably with one-click copy.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| code | `string` | — | yes | Raw code to display. |
| language | `string` | `tsx` | no | Prism language identifier. |
| showCopyButton | `boolean` | `true` | no | Show/hide the copy control. |

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
<CodeBlock code={sourceCode} language="ts" />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not nest CodeBlock in Response code fences manually** — Response already routes fenced code to CodeBlock.

## Accessibility

- **Copy button**: Icon-labeled button with aria-label that flips to Copied.

---

# CommandPalette

Cmd+K style command palette with lexical search, sectioned results and full keyboard navigation

> Import: `import { CommandPalette } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/command-palette.json
> Tier: organism · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

AI-assisted and power-user apps expose many actions; a command palette keeps them all one keystroke away. The palette is a combobox+listbox with aria-activedescendant navigation so focus never leaves the input, filters lexically over labels/sections/keywords, and reports selection through a single callback.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| open | `boolean` | — | yes | Whether the palette is visible (controlled) |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` | — | yes | Called when the user opens or dismisses the palette |
| commands | `Command[]` | — | yes | Available commands: { id, label, section?, keywords?, shortcut? } |
| onSelect | `(command: Command) => void` | — | yes | Invoked with the chosen command before the palette closes |
| placeholder | `string` | `Type a command.` | no | Input placeholder text |
| loadCommands | `(query: string) => Promise<Command[]>` | — | no | Async command source; debounced and stale-response guarded. |
| debounceMs | `number` | `200` | no | Debounce for loadCommands in ms. |
| renderCommand | `(command, state: { active: boolean }) => ReactNode` | — | no | Custom row renderer (icons, type badges). |
| loadingText | `string` | — | no | Shown while async commands load. |

## Examples

### Wired to Cmd+K

Toggle the palette with Cmd/Ctrl+K and run the selected command.

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

useEffect(() => {
  const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && event.key === 'k') {
      event.preventDefault();
      setOpen((current) => !current);
    }
  };
  window.addEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);
  return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);
}, []);

<CommandPalette
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  commands={commands}
  onSelect={(command) => run(command.id)}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not use the palette as a text editor command** — The palette searches discrete commands. For AI chat input use PromptInput instead.

## Accessibility

- **Combobox pattern**: The input uses role=combobox with aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant and aria-autocomplete=list.
- **Keyboard navigation**: Arrow keys cycle options, Enter selects, Escape closes; focus never leaves the input.
- **Option semantics**: Each result is role=option with aria-selected marking the active item.

## Composition

- Compose with **PromptInput** — CommandPalette switches modes/actions; PromptInput captures free-form chat text.
- Related: PromptInput, Dialog

---

# ConfirmDialog

Accessible confirmation dialog with async pending state, destructive variant and cancellable actions, built on Dialog.

> Import: `import { ConfirmDialog } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/confirm-dialog.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Confirmations are copy-pasted per project (79 hand-rolled modals in the audited apps), usually without focus trapping or Escape. ConfirmDialog provides the accessible default plus a pending state for async actions.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| open | `boolean` | — | yes | Controlled visibility. |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` | — | yes | Open/close requests. |
| title | `string` | — | yes | Dialog title (accessible name). |
| description | `string` | — | no | Supporting line under the title. |
| confirmLabel | `string` | `Confirm` | no | Confirm button label. |
| cancelLabel | `string` | `Cancel` | no | Cancel button label. |
| destructive | `boolean` | `false` | no | Red confirm button for destructive actions. |
| onConfirm | `() => void | Promise<void>` | — | yes | Confirm handler; a promise shows a pending state. |
| closeOnConfirm | `boolean` | `true` | no | Close when the confirm handler resolves. |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | no | Extra body content above the actions. |

## Examples

### Delete confirmation

Async-safe destructive confirmation.

```tsx
<ConfirmDialog
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title="Delete project"
  description="This cannot be undone."
  destructive
  confirmLabel="Delete"
  onConfirm={deleteProject}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use it for multi-field forms** — ConfirmDialog is a yes/no gate; richer flows belong in Dialog.

## Accessibility

- **Modal semantics**: Inherits Dialog's focus trap, Escape, backdrop and focus restoration
- **Pending state**: Confirm shows aria-busy while the promise runs; dismissal is blocked

## Composition

- Compose with **Dialog** — Built on Dialog; use Dialog directly for custom layouts
  
  ```tsx
  <ConfirmDialog … />
  ```
- Related: Dialog, Button, Alert

---

# Confirmation

Human-in-the-loop approval gate for agent actions. Pauses execution until the user approves or rejects.

> Import: `import { Confirmation } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/confirmation.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

Make destructive or consequential tool calls require explicit user consent.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| title | `string` | — | yes | Summary of the action requiring approval. |
| description | `string` | — | no | Detail: affected resource or risk note. |
| toolName | `string` | — | no | Tool/action name shown as mono text. |
| status | `'pending' | 'approved' | 'rejected'` | `pending` | no | Controlled outcome; omit for uncontrolled. |
| variant | `'default' | 'warning' | 'destructive' | 'info' | 'success'` | `default` | no | Accent color of the pending card; outcome chips always follow the result. |
| onApprove | `() => void` | — | no | Called on approval. |
| onReject | `() => void` | — | no | Called on rejection. |
| labels | `object` | — | no | Overrides for approve/reject/approved/rejected labels. |
| approveVariant | `'default' | 'destructive' | 'outline' | 'secondary' | 'ghost' | 'link'` | `default` | no | Button variant for the approve action. |
| rejectVariant | `'default' | 'destructive' | 'outline' | 'secondary' | 'ghost' | 'link'` | `outline` | no | Button variant for the reject action. |
| showActions | `boolean` | `true` | no | Hide the action buttons (controlled-only gate; status drives the chip). |

## Examples

### Gate a destructive tool

```tsx
<Confirmation title="Delete all files?" toolName="delete_all" onApprove={run} onReject={cancel} />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not auto-approve after timeout** — Silent approval defeats the safety purpose; keep waiting or fail explicitly.

## Accessibility

- **Dialog semantics**: Pending state renders role=alertdialog labeled by the title.
- **Outcome announcement**: Status chip text announces Approved/Rejected.

---

# Conversation

A container for displaying a list of chat messages with auto-scroll and loading states

> Import: `import { Conversation } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/conversation.json
> Tier: organism · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

The Conversation component manages the display of multiple messages in a chat interface. It handles auto-scrolling to show new messages, distinct avatar configurations for users and assistants, and a loading state when the AI is generating a response.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| messages | `Message[]` | — | yes | Array of message objects to display |
| showAvatars | `boolean` | `true` | no | Whether to show avatars for messages |
| userAvatarSrc | `string` | — | no | Custom avatar image URL for user messages |
| userAvatarFallback | `string` | — | no | Fallback text for user avatar |
| assistantAvatarSrc | `string` | — | no | Custom avatar image URL for assistant messages |
| assistantAvatarFallback | `string` | — | no | Fallback text for assistant avatar |
| isLoading | `boolean` | `false` | no | Whether the assistant is currently generating a response |
| loadingMessage | `string` | `Thinking...` | no | Text to display while loading |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply to the conversation container |
| renderContent | `(content: string) => ReactNode` | — | no | Custom renderer applied to every message (e.g. markdown). |
| streamingMessageId | `string` | — | no | ID of the message still generating; renders its streaming cursor and auto-scrolls. |
| showScrollButton | `boolean` | `true` | no | Show the scroll-to-latest button when the user scrolls up |
| showDownload | `boolean` | `true` | no | Show the transcript download action |
| messageErrors | `Record<string, string>` | — | no | Map of message id to error text; renders an error card on that message |
| onRetryMessage | `(message: MessageData) => void` | — | no | Called when the user retries a failed message |
| welcomeTitle | `string` | — | no | Title shown in the empty/welcome state |
| welcomeDescription | `string` | — | no | Supporting text in the welcome state |
| welcomeSuggestions | `string[]` | — | no | Starter prompts shown in the welcome state |
| onWelcomeSelect | `(prompt: string) => void` | — | no | Called when a welcome suggestion is clicked |
| hasMoreHistory | `boolean` | — | no | Whether older history pages exist (enables infinite scroll) |
| isLoadingMore | `boolean` | — | no | Whether a history page is currently loading |
| onLoadMore | `() => void` | — | no | Called when the user scrolls to the top to load older messages |

## Examples

### Basic conversation

Simple conversation with user and assistant messages

```tsx
<Conversation 
  messages={[
    { id: '1', role: 'user', content: 'Hello' },
    { id: '2', role: 'assistant', content: 'Hi there!' }
  ]}
/>
```

### With custom avatars

Conversation with custom avatar images and fallbacks

```tsx
<Conversation 
  messages={messages}
  userAvatarSrc="/user.png"
  userAvatarFallback="JD"
  assistantAvatarSrc="/ai.png"
  assistantAvatarFallback="AI"
/>
```

### With loading state

Conversation showing loading indicator while AI responds

```tsx
<Conversation 
  messages={messages}
  isLoading={true}
  loadingMessage="Generating your response..."
/>
```

### Without avatars

More compact conversation without avatars

```tsx
<Conversation 
  messages={messages}
  showAvatars={false}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't manage state inside Conversation** — Conversation should be a controlled component. State should be managed by the parent.
- **Don't use for non-chat content** — Conversation is specifically for chat messages, not general data display

## Accessibility

- **Live regions**: Consider adding aria-live to the container for screen readers to announce new messages
- **Keyboard navigation**: Container is scrollable with keyboard. Focus management depends on parent component
- **Loading announcement**: Loading state is visually indicated but not announced to screen readers by default

## Composition

- Compose with **Message** — Conversation renders multiple Message components internally
  
  ```tsx
  Conversation maps over messages array and renders Message for each item
  ```
- Compose with **PromptInput** — PromptInput is typically used alongside Conversation to submit new messages
  
  ```tsx
  Conversation displays messages, PromptInput adds new ones to the messages array
  ```
- Related: Message, PromptInput, ChatLayout

---

# DataTable

Config-driven table: one component plus a columns config that owns shape, sorting, pagination, and row interaction.

> Import: `import { DataTable } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/data-table.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Most tables are 90% configuration — columns, sortability, page size, row click. DataTable collapses that into a single columns config so application code describes WHAT the table shows, not HOW to render th/td/sort/paginate markup by hand, while keeping full control through cell renderers.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| columns | `DataTableColumn<T>[]` | — | yes | Column configuration: key, header, optional cell renderer, sortable flag, align, className. Each column may define onClick(row) to make the cell content a button (column-level callbacks); onSortChange wires server-side sorting. |
| data | `T[]` | — | yes | Row data. |
| rowId | `(row: T) => string` | — | yes | Stable id per row (React key + test hooks). |
| caption | `string` | — | no | Accessible table caption. |
| defaultSort | `{ key: string; dir: 'asc' | 'desc' } | null` | — | no | Initial sort when uncontrolled. |
| sortKey | `string | null` | — | no | Controlled sort column (pair with sortDir and onSortChange). |
| sortDir | `'asc' | 'desc'` | — | no | Controlled sort direction. |
| onSortChange | `(key: string, dir: 'asc' | 'desc') => void` | — | no | Fires when a sortable header is toggled (controlled or not). |
| pageSize | `number` | — | no | Rows per page; enables pagination with a count line when set. |
| page | `number` | — | no | Controlled page number (1-based) when pageSize is set. |
| onPageChange | `(page: number) => void` | — | no | Fires when the pagination control changes page. |
| onRowClick | `(row: T) => void` | — | no | Makes rows interactive: click plus Enter/Space activation with ring focus. |
| renderSortIcon | `(state: 'none' | 'asc' | 'desc') => ReactNode` | — | no | Replace the default ▲/▼/↕ header glyphs with custom markup. |
| stickyHeader | `boolean` | `false` | no | Pin the header while the body scrolls (add a max-height via className). |
| density | `'default' | 'compact'` | `default` | no | Row density — compact shrinks text and cell padding. |
| zebra | `boolean` | `false` | no | Zebra-striped rows for long tables. |
| loading | `boolean` | `false` | no | Render skeleton placeholder rows (tbody is aria-busy while loading). |
| loadingRows | `number` | — | no | Skeleton row count while loading (defaults to page size, else 5) — match it to visible data so rows do not jump. |
| emptyMessage | `string` | `'No results.'` | no | Shown when data is empty. |
| selectAllLabel | `string` | `'Select all rows'` | no | Accessible label for the select-all checkbox. |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional classes for the table wrapper. |
| selectedRowIds | `string[]` | — | no | Selected row ids (controlled) — enables the leading selection column. |
| onSelectedRowIdsChange | `(ids: string[]) => void` | — | no | Fires after a row or select-all toggle. |
| isRowSelectable | `(row: T) => boolean` | — | no | Disable selection for individual rows. |
| bulkActions | `ReactNode` | — | no | Rendered above the table while rows are selected. |
| manualPagination | `boolean` | `false` | no | Server pagination: render data as-is, do not slice or sort. |
| total | `number` | — | no | Total row count across pages (summary + derived page count). |
| pageCount | `number` | — | no | Total page count (manual pagination). |

## Examples

### Sortable, paginated table from one config

Sorting, paging, empty state, and row interaction come from the config — no table markup.

```tsx
<DataTable
  caption="Recent conversations"
  columns={[
    { key: 'title', header: 'Title', sortable: true },
    { key: 'messages', header: 'Messages', align: 'right', sortable: true },
    { key: 'updatedAt', header: 'Updated', cell: (row) => row.updatedAt.toLocaleDateString() },
  ]}
  data={conversations}
  rowId={(row) => row.id}
  pageSize={10}
  onRowClick={(row) => router.push(`/c/${row.id}`)}
/>
```

### Controlled sort (server-side)

Pass sort props + onSortChange to let the backend own ordering; DataTable renders aria-sort either way.

```tsx
<DataTable
  columns={columns}
  data={rows}
  rowId={(row) => row.id}
  sortKey={sort.key}
  sortDir={sort.dir}
  onSortChange={(key, dir) => fetchSorted(key, dir)}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't sort server-owned data locally** — Local sorting runs on the rows you pass in. When data is paged by the API, wire onSortChange to a server query — sorting one page locally lies about global order.
- **Don't put heavy interactions in onRowClick only** — Rows are keyboard-focusable when onRowClick is set (Enter/Space activate), but a row click is not a semantic action for assistive tech. Also provide a real link/button (e.g. in a cell) for primary navigation.
- **Don't build nested tables for layout** — DataTable is for tabular DATA. Layout grids belong to Card/grid containers — nested tables degrade the table navigation story for screen readers.

## Accessibility

- **Sortable headers**: Sortable th elements carry aria-sort (ascending/descending/none) and use a real button for the toggle
- **Caption**: Renders a native <caption> naming the table's purpose
- **Row interaction**: With onRowClick rows are tabIndex=0 and activate on Enter/Space with a visible ring
- **Pagination feedback**: The result count line is aria-live=polite and pagination reuses the Pagination nav (aria-current=page)

## Composition

- Compose with **Pagination** — Used internally when pageSize is set — you never need to wire it yourself
  
  ```tsx
  <DataTable pageSize={10} … /> // pagination + count render automatically
  ```
- Compose with **Badge / Button** — Use column cell renderers for status pills and row actions
  
  ```tsx
  { key: 'status', header: 'Status', cell: (row) => <Badge variant={row.ok ? 'default' : 'destructive'}>{row.status}</Badge> }
  ```
- Compose with **Table** — Prefer Table when you need fully custom markup or non-interactive static data
- Related: Table, Pagination, Badge, Skeleton

---

# DatePicker

Native date field with an ISO-string contract, min/max passthrough and an optional clear button.

> Import: `import { DatePicker } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/date-picker.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

A custom calendar is a large accessibility surface. The platform date picker already handles locale formatting, keyboard editing and mobile wheels, so DatePicker standardizes the ISO contract and a clear affordance instead of reimplementing a calendar.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| value | `string` | — | no | ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD), controlled. |
| defaultValue | `string` | — | no | ISO date, initial value. |
| onValueChange | `(value: string) => void` | — | no | Fired with the ISO string; '' when cleared. |
| clearable | `boolean` | `false` | no | Shows a clear button once a value exists. |

## Examples

### ISO date field

Controlled ISO value with a clear button.

```tsx
<DatePicker
  aria-label="Start date"
  value={start}
  onValueChange={setStart}
  clearable
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't store locale-formatted strings** — The contract is YYYY-MM-DD; format for display at the edge.

## Accessibility

- **Platform input**: Renders input[type=date] so OS pickers and keyboard editing apply

## Composition

- Compose with **FormField** — Wrap for label/hint/error wiring
  
  ```tsx
  <FormField id="start" label="Start date"><DatePicker /></FormField>
  ```
- Related: TimePicker, FormField, Input

---

# Dialog

Accessible modal dialog with focus trap/restore, backdrop and Escape dismissal, size presets, optional header/footer slots, a scrollable body, and opt-in fade motion.

> Import: `import { Dialog } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/dialog.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Modals interrupt the task flow on purpose: confirmations, small forms, and destructive-action guards. The Dialog implements the full modal contract — aria-modal labelling, initial focus, a Tab focus trap, Escape and backdrop dismissal, and focus restoration to the opener — so consumers never hand-roll focus management.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| open | `boolean` | — | yes | Whether the dialog is visible (controlled) |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` | — | yes | Called when the user requests open/close (escape, backdrop, close button) |
| title | `string` | — | no | Accessible name + default header title. Optional when composing a custom header with ariaLabel. |
| description | `string` | — | no | Optional supporting text, wired via aria-describedby |
| closeOnBackdrop | `boolean` | `true` | no | Whether clicking the backdrop closes the dialog |
| initialFocusRef | `React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null>` | — | no | Element focused on open; defaults to the first focusable element |
| ariaLabel | `string` | — | no | Accessible label for the dialog (required for screen readers) |
| showClose | `boolean` | `true` | no | Hide the close (?) button in the header; Escape and backdrop still close. |
| closeLabel | `string` | `'Close dialog'` | no | Accessible label for the close button. |
| animate | `boolean` | `false` | no | Fade the backdrop and panel in/out on open/close (needs tailwindcss-animate; reduced motion respected). |
| size | `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl'` | `md` | no | Panel max-width preset. |
| header | `ReactNode` | — | no | Replaces the default header row — compose with DialogHeader/DialogTitle/DialogDescription (ids wire automatically). |
| footer | `ReactNode` | — | no | Action row pinned under the body. |
| scrollable | `boolean` | `false` | no | Caps the body height and scrolls inside the panel. |
| bodyClassName | `string` | — | no | Extra classes for the body wrapper. |

## Examples

### Destructive confirmation

Controlled dialog; the opener keeps the open state.

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Dialog
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title="Delete project?"
  description="This cannot be undone."
>
  <button onClick={confirmDelete}>Delete</button>
</Dialog>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not open a dialog without a focusable control** — Users must be able to act or dismiss without a mouse. Always include at least one button inside the dialog body.

## Accessibility

- **Modal semantics**: role=dialog with aria-modal=true, aria-labelledby from the title, and aria-describedby when a description is provided.
- **Focus management**: Initial focus moves into the dialog; Tab wraps between focusable elements; focus returns to the opener on close.
- **Escape dismissal**: Escape closes the dialog via the onOpenChange callback.

## Composition

- Compose with **Button** — Dialog footers use Button for primary/secondary actions.
  
  ```tsx
  <Dialog ...><Button onClick={onConfirm}>Confirm</Button></Dialog>
  ```
- Related: Button, Toast, Drawer, Confirmation

---

# Drawer

Edge sheet for secondary flows: slides from any side (sm/md/lg), with Dialog-grade modal semantics (portal, focus trap, Escape, focus restoration).

> Import: `import { Drawer } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/drawer.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Filters, detail panes, and mobile navigation need more room than a popover but shouldn't hijack the whole screen like a dialog. Drawer is an edge-anchored sheet with the SAME a11y contract as Dialog — portal, aria-modal, focus trap, Escape, focus restore — so swapping between them never regresses keyboard or screen-reader behavior.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| open | `boolean` | — | yes | Whether the drawer is visible (controlled). |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` | — | yes | Close requests (✕, Escape, backdrop, your own triggers). |
| title | `string` | — | yes | Accessible dialog name rendered as the header title. |
| description | `string` | — | no | Supporting line under the title (wired via aria-describedby). |
| side | `'left' | 'right' | 'top' | 'bottom'` | `right` | no | Edge the drawer slides from. |
| size | `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl'` | `md` | no | Preset extent along the side axis (width for left/right, height for top/bottom). |
| width | `number | string` | — | no | Custom extent for left/right drawers: pixels (480) or any CSS length ("70vw"). Overrides size. |
