| height | `number | string` | — | no | Custom extent for top/bottom drawers: pixels (320) or any CSS length ("60vh"). Overrides size. |
| closeOnBackdrop | `boolean` | `true` | no | Clicking the backdrop closes the drawer. |
| showClose | `boolean` | `true` | no | Hide the header ✕ button (Escape and backdrop still close). |
| closeLabel | `string` | `'Close drawer'` | no | Accessible label for the close button. |
| initialFocusRef | `RefObject<HTMLElement | null>` | — | no | Element focused on open (defaults to the first focusable element). |
| ariaLabel | `string` | — | no | Overrides the accessible name (defaults to the title). |
| animate | `boolean` | `false` | no | Slide the panel in from its edge and out on close (needs tailwindcss-animate; reduced motion respected). |

## Examples

### Filter panel from the right

The workhorse: side panel that keeps context visible.

```tsx
<Button onClick={() => setFiltersOpen(true)}>Filters</Button>
<Drawer
  open={filtersOpen}
  onOpenChange={setFiltersOpen}
  title="Filter results"
  description="Narrow by status and date"
  side="right"
  size="md"
>
  <FilterControls />
</Drawer>
```

### Mobile navigation from the bottom

```tsx
<Drawer open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Jump to" side="bottom" size="sm">
  <nav className="flex flex-col gap-2">
    <a href="/docs">Docs</a>
    <a href="/docs/components">Components</a>
  </nav>
</Drawer>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use a Drawer for a single decision** — One-question gates belong in Confirmation (alertdialog) — a whole sheet for approve/reject buries the decision.
- **Don't stack sheets** — Two open drawers fight for focus and z-index. Close the first (or render one container) before opening another.
- **Don't hide critical actions in a closed drawer** — Drawers are secondary flows — the primary action must stay visible on the page.

## Accessibility

- **Modal dialog semantics**: role=dialog + aria-modal, labelled by title, described by description; portal to body
- **Focus management**: Focus moves to the first focusable element on open, is trapped with Tab/Shift+Tab, and restores to the opener on close
- **Dismissal parity with Dialog**: Escape closes; backdrop click closes when closeOnBackdrop (default)
- **Scroll containment**: Body region scrolls internally (overflow-y-auto) — the page behind never scrolls

## Composition

- Compose with **Button** — The trigger that opens the drawer (aria-haspopup optional)
  
  ```tsx
  <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Filters</Button>
  ```
- Compose with **Form / FormLayout / FormField** — Drawers commonly host forms — spacing and wiring come from the form family
  
  ```tsx
  <Drawer …><FormLayout layout="stack">…</FormLayout></Drawer>
  ```
- Compose with **Dialog** — Dialog for centered modal decisions; Drawer for edge-anchored secondary flows
- Related: Dialog, Popover, Form

---

# EmptyState

Placeholder for empty collections, zero-result searches and unconfigured features, with title, description and action slots.

> Import: `import { EmptyState } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/empty-state.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Empty states are where users decide what to do next. A consistent icon/title/description/action hierarchy beats ad-hoc 'No data' strings, and a stable structure is easier for screen readers and tests.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| title | `string` | — | yes | Primary message. |
| description | `string` | — | no | Supporting line explaining the next step. |
| icon | `ReactNode` | — | no | Decorative icon/illustration above the title. |
| action | `ReactNode` | — | no | Primary action (Button or link). |
| secondaryAction | `ReactNode` | — | no | Secondary action beside the primary one. |
| size | `'sm' | 'md'` | `md` | no | Compact padding for panels/table bodies. |

## Examples

### Empty collection

Title, explanation and one primary action.

```tsx
<EmptyState
  title="No classes yet"
  description="Create your first class to get started."
  action={<Button>New class</Button>}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use it for errors** — Empty is a normal state; failures need Alert/ErrorAlert with retry affordances.

## Accessibility

- **Action targets**: Actions are whatever you pass — use Button/link components so they stay focusable and announced

## Composition

- Compose with **Card** — Often rendered inside a Card body or a DataTable empty slot
  
  ```tsx
  <Card><CardContent><EmptyState … /></CardContent></Card>
  ```
- Related: Alert, Card, DataTable

---

# Fieldset

Groups related form controls in a native fieldset with a legend, optional description, and an error slot.

> Import: `import { Fieldset } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/fieldset.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Radio groups, checkbox groups, and multi-control sections need an accessible group name. Fieldset provides the native <fieldset>/<legend> semantics with token-based styling (borderless by default) plus description and error slots so related controls read as one unit.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| legend | `string` | — | no | Legend rendered as the group's accessible name. |
| description | `string` | — | no | Muted supporting line rendered under the legend. |
| error | `string` | — | no | Error line rendered under the controls; announced via role=alert. |

## Examples

### Grouped radio-style options

Legend names the group; description adds context.

```tsx
<Fieldset legend="Export format" description="Applied to every selected row">
  <Checkbox id="csv" /><Label htmlFor="csv">CSV</Label>
  <Checkbox id="json" /><Label htmlFor="json">JSON</Label>
</Fieldset>
```

### With a group-level error

Errors that belong to the whole group live on the fieldset, not each control.

```tsx
<Fieldset legend="Visibility" error="Choose who can see this project">
  <RadioGroupItem value="private" label="Private" />
  <RadioGroupItem value="team" label="Team" />
</Fieldset>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use a fieldset for layout grouping** — Fieldset is for FORM controls that share one accessible name. For purely visual grouping use Card or a plain div — screen readers announce every fieldset as a landmark-ish group and excess ones add noise.
- **Don't skip the legend** — A fieldset without legend (or without aria-label) leaves the group unnamed — controls inside lose their grouping context for screen reader users.

## Accessibility

- **Native group semantics**: Renders <fieldset> with <legend>; the legend is the group's accessible name announced before each control
- **Group-level errors**: The error slot renders with role=alert so it is announced when it appears

## Composition

- Compose with **RadioGroup / Checkbox** — Wrap mutually exclusive or multi-select controls so their group name is announced
  
  ```tsx
  <Fieldset legend="Plan"><RadioGroup name="plan">…</RadioGroup></Fieldset>
  ```
- Compose with **FormField** — For a single labeled control prefer FormField; Fieldset is for GROUPS of controls
- Related: Radio, Checkbox, FormField, Label

---

# FileUpload

Drag-and-drop file picker with a removable file list and per-file progress bars.

> Import: `import { FileUpload } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/file-upload.json
> Tier: organism · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

File inputs are hard to style and easy to make inaccessible. FileUpload keeps the native input as the real control, adds a drop zone as an enhancement, and exposes plain File objects so the transport and progress stay yours.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| files | `File[]` | — | no | Controlled selection. |
| defaultFiles | `File[]` | — | no | Initial selection when uncontrolled. |
| onFilesChange | `(files: File[]) => void` | — | no | Fired on add, drop, remove. |
| label | `string` | `Drop files here or click to browse` | no | Drop-zone copy. |
| hint | `string` | — | no | Helper line under the drop zone. |
| progress | `Record<string, number>` | — | no | Per-file progress 0-100 keyed by file name; renders progress bars. |

## Examples

### Attachments with progress

Native input + drop zone + progress.

```tsx
<FileUpload
  aria-label="Attachments"
  accept=".pdf,.csv"
  progress={{ 'report.pdf': 42 }}
  onFilesChange={setFiles}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't hide the input from the a11y tree** — The label targets the real input, keeping keyboard and mobile file dialogs working.

## Accessibility

- **Native control**: Visible label targets a real (sr-only) file input
- **Progress**: Each uploading file exposes role=progressbar with a name

## Composition

- Compose with **FormField** — Wrap for label/error wiring
  
  ```tsx
  <FormField id="files" label="Attachments"><FileUpload /></FormField>
  ```
- Related: Attachment, FormField, Progress

---

# FilterBar

List-page filter strip: search field, filter controls, reset affordance and trailing actions.

> Import: `import { FilterBar } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/filter-bar.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Filter rows drift: some pages wrap, some scroll, resets appear inconsistently. FilterBar fixes the order (search → filters → reset → trailing) and keeps the strip compact on narrow screens.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| searchValue | `string` | — | no | Controlled search text. |
| onSearchChange | `(value: string) => void` | — | no | Fires on each keystroke; hides the search box when omitted. |
| searchPlaceholder | `string` | `Search…` | no | Search input placeholder (also its accessible name). |
| onReset | `() => void` | — | no | Shows a reset button when provided. |
| activeCount | `number` | `0` | no | Active filter count appended to the reset label. |
| trailing | `ReactNode` | — | no | Far-right actions (bulk actions, column settings). |

## Examples

### List filters

Search, filters, reset and count in one strip.

```tsx
<FilterBar
  searchValue={query}
  onSearchChange={setQuery}
  searchPlaceholder="Search students"
  onReset={resetFilters}
  activeCount={activeFilters}
>
  <Select label="Status" options={statusOptions} />
</FilterBar>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't put the primary action in the bar** — FilterBar is for narrowing; creation actions belong in PageHeader actions.

## Accessibility

- **Search landmark**: Wraps controls in role=search; the search input is labelled by its placeholder

## Composition

- Compose with **Select** — Filter controls render in children
  
  ```tsx
  <FilterBar><Select … /></FilterBar>
  ```
- Related: DataTable, Select, Input, PageHeader

---

# Flex / FlexItem

Typed flexbox container (direction/align/justify/wrap/gap) with FlexItem for per-child grow/shrink/basis controls.

> Import: `import { Flex } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/flex.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Layout utilities should be discoverable and tokenized: Flex turns display:flex into named props with token gaps, so spacing comes from the design system instead of scattered arbitrary classes. FlexItem handles per-child flex values through style (not runtime-built classes) so nothing gets purged from the stylesheet.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| direction | `'row' | 'column'` | `row` | no | Main axis direction. |
| align | `'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'stretch' | 'baseline'` | — | no | Cross-axis alignment (align-items; align-self on FlexItem). |
| justify | `'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'between' | 'around' | 'evenly'` | — | no | Main-axis distribution (justify-content). |
| wrap | `boolean` | `false` | no | Allow items to wrap onto multiple lines. |
| gap | `'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl'` | `md` | no | Token gap between children. |
| as | `'div' | 'span' | 'section' | 'article' | 'nav' | 'header' | 'footer' | 'li'` | — | no | Semantic element (FlexItem also supports 'li', Flex supports the structural elements). |
| grow | `boolean | string` | — | no | flex-grow for this FlexItem (true = 1, or a numeric string). |
| shrink | `boolean | string` | — | no | flex-shrink for this FlexItem (false = 0, or a numeric string). |
| basis | `string` | — | no | flex-basis for this FlexItem (e.g. '0', '200px', 'auto'). |

## Examples

### Toolbar row

Token gaps keep spacing on the design system grid.

```tsx
<Flex align="center" justify="between" gap="sm">
  <Text size="sm" weight="medium">Title</Text>
  <Flex gap="sm">
    <Button size="sm" variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>
    <Button size="sm">Save</Button>
  </Flex>
</Flex>
```

### Sidebar + content

FlexItem values render via inline style — arbitrary numeric utilities would be purged.

```tsx
<Flex gap="lg">
  <FlexItem basis="240px" shrink={false}>
    <SidebarNav />
  </FlexItem>
  <FlexItem grow>
    <Article />
  </FlexItem>
</Flex>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't rebuild layout primitives with arbitrary classes** — Runtime-built class strings (grow-[${value}]) never make it into the compiled CSS. Use Flex/FlexItem props — they emit style values where Tailwind can't.
- **Don't wrap a single child** — A Flex with one child adds a pointless layout layer — use Block with utilities instead.

## Accessibility

- **Layout-only semantics**: Renders div/span/section… — no interactive or live behavior is added
- **Wrap keeps reading order**: flex-wrap reflows visually; DOM order (reading order) never changes

## Composition

- Compose with **Grid** — Flex for one-axis alignment; Grid for two-axis layout
- Compose with **Block** — Blocks are the semantic wrappers Flex arranges
- Related: Grid, Block, List

---

# Form

Semantic form element with even-spacing layouts: stacked (default), bordered card, or inline row — native submit and validation untouched.

> Import: `import { Form } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/form.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Forms need two things the DOM gives you: a real <form> (submit, Enter, validation) and even, tokenized spacing between fields. Form bakes the layout into variants so field rhythm stays consistent without wrapper divs or one-off gap classes.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| variant | `'default' | 'card' | 'inline'` | `default` | no | Visual container: plain vertical stack, bordered card, or inline row with aligned ends. |
| gap | `'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | number` | — | no | Even spacing between children — token ('md' default) or exact pixels (16). |
| onSubmit | `(event: React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => void` | — | no | Native submit handler — Enter in a text input submits like any form. |
| noValidate | `boolean` | `false` | no | Skip native validation when you drive errors through FormField error props. |

## Examples

### Stacked settings form

Fields space evenly on the md token; errors come from FormField.

```tsx
<Form onSubmit={save} noValidate className="max-w-md">
  <FormField id="name" label="Display name" error={errors.name} required>
    <Input value={name} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} />
  </FormField>
  <FormField id="email" label="Email" error={errors.email}>
    <Input type="email" value={email} onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)} />
  </FormField>
  <Button type="submit">Save settings</Button>
</Form>
```

### Card and inline variants

```tsx
<Form variant="card" gap={16}>…</Form>

<Form variant="inline" onSubmit={search}>
  <FormField id="q" label="Search"><Input type="search" /></FormField>
  <Button type="submit">Go</Button>
</Form>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't nest forms** — Nested <form> elements are invalid HTML — browsers drop the inner form's submit association. Compose with FormLayout sections instead.
- **Don't fight native validation blindly** — Passing noValidate means YOU own every error message — pair it with FormField error props or keep native validation on.

## Accessibility

- **Native form semantics**: Renders <form> — Enter-to-submit, browser validation, and autocomplete all work
- **Even spacing is tokenized**: gap defaults to the md token and accepts exact pixels — rhythm stays consistent across forms

## Composition

- Compose with **FormField** — Each field is a FormField; Form spaces them evenly
  
  ```tsx
  <Form onSubmit={save}><FormField …>…</FormField></Form>
  ```
- Compose with **FormLayout** — Multi-column or grouped sections inside a form
- Compose with **Button** — Submit button with type="submit" — native Enter handling comes free
- Related: FormField, FormLayout, Fieldset, Input

---

# FormField

Label + control + hint/error in one unit with htmlFor, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid wiring applied automatically.

> Import: `import { FormField } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/form-field.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Every form control needs the same trio — label, hint or error, correct ARIA wiring — and hand-wiring it is where accessibility regressions start. FormField clones id/aria-describedby/aria-invalid onto a single-element child so the common case is one component and zero boilerplate.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| id | `string` | — | yes | The control's id — shared with the label's htmlFor and the hint/error ids. |
| label | `string` | — | yes | Visible label text (kept for screen readers even when labelHidden). |
| hint | `string` | — | no | Helper text under the control, wired via aria-describedby. |
| error | `string` | — | no | Validation error; replaces the hint, sets aria-invalid on the control, announced via role=alert. |
| required | `boolean` | `false` | no | Renders the required marker next to the label. |
| labelHidden | `boolean` | `false` | no | Keeps the label screen-reader visible but hides it visually (sr-only). |
| trailing | `ReactNode` | — | no | Slot pinned to the far right of the label row (badge, link, action). |
| tooltip | `string` | — | no | Info icon rendered after the label; opens a tooltip with this text. |
| labelPlacement | `'top' | 'left'` | `top` | no | Stack the label above the control (default) or inline it to the left. |

## Examples

### Text input with hint

The cloned child receives id, aria-describedby, and the label pairs via htmlFor.

```tsx
<FormField id="email" label="Email address" hint="We never share your email" required>
  <Input type="email" autoComplete="email" />
</FormField>
```

### Error state

Error replaces the hint, flips aria-invalid on the control, and announces via role=alert.

```tsx
<FormField id="email" label="Email address" error={errors.email} required>
  <Input type="email" value={email} onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)} />
</FormField>
```

### Search-style field

```tsx
<FormField id="assignee" label="Assign to" hint="Start typing to filter">
  <Search options={people} onValueChange={setAssignee} />
</FormField>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't rely on placeholder as the label** — Placeholders disappear on input and fail color-contrast rules. FormField renders a real <Label>; use placeholder only for example format.
- **Don't nest multiple controls in one FormField** — The aria wiring (describedby/invalid) clones onto exactly one child element. For groups, use Fieldset or one FormField per control.
- **Don't duplicate ids across fields** — id keys the whole wiring — every FormField in a form must receive a unique id and the child must not override it with a different value.

## Accessibility

- **Label association**: Renders <Label htmlFor={id}> and clones the same id onto single-element children
- **Hint and error wiring**: aria-describedby points at the hint (or the error when present); errors render with role=alert
- **Invalid state**: Sets aria-invalid on the cloned control when error is present
- **Required marker**: The asterisk is aria-hidden; native required semantics come from the control's own required attribute

## Composition

- Compose with **Input / Textarea / Select / Search / Autocomplete** — Wrap exactly one control — id/aria wiring is cloned onto it automatically
  
  ```tsx
  <FormField id="email" label="Email"><Input type="email" /></FormField>
  ```
- Compose with **Fieldset** — Use Fieldset (not FormField) when the label names a GROUP of controls
- Related: Label, Input, Fieldset, Search, Autocomplete

---

# FormLayout

Groups form fields with even, tokenized spacing: vertical stack, horizontal row, or 1-4 column grid, optionally as a semantic fieldset.

> Import: `import { FormLayout } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/form-layout.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Field rhythm is the difference between a form that scans and one that doesn't. FormLayout owns the ARRANGEMENT (stack/row/grid + exact gap) while Fieldset owns the group semantics (legend) and FormField owns per-control wiring — three small pieces instead of one magic wrapper.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| layout | `'stack' | 'row' | 'grid'` | `stack` | no | Grouping layout: even vertical stack, horizontal row, or column grid. |
| columns | `1 | 2 | 3 | 4` | `2` | no | Grid column count (literal classes survive CSS purging). |
| gap | `'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | number` | — | no | Even spacing between children — token or exact pixels (16). |
| legend | `string` | — | no | Group label rendered as a semantic <legend> (fieldset mode). |
| description | `string` | — | no | Supporting line under the legend (fieldset mode). |
| as | `'div' | 'fieldset'` | `div` | no | Render as a semantic fieldset when the layout names a group of controls. |

## Examples

### Two-column settings grid

Exact 16px gaps; fields wrap into rows of two.

```tsx
<FormLayout layout="grid" columns={2} gap={16} as="fieldset" legend="Profile">
  <FormField id="first" label="First name"><Input /></FormField>
  <FormField id="last" label="Last name"><Input /></FormField>
  <FormField id="email" label="Email"><Input type="email" /></FormField>
</FormLayout>
```

### Inline action row

```tsx
<FormLayout layout="row" gap="sm">
  <FormField id="q" label="Search"><Input type="search" /></FormField>
  <Button type="submit">Go</Button>
</FormLayout>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't hand-roll spacer divs** — Empty divs with heights drift from the token scale and break under different densities — gap exists for spacing.
- **Don't use fieldset mode without a legend** — as="fieldset" without legend renders an unnamed group — assistive tech announces nothing useful. Prefer div, or provide the legend.

## Accessibility

- **Fieldset mode gives the group a name**: legend renders as a real <legend>; use it whenever the layout wraps related controls
- **Reading order equals DOM order**: Row/grid layouts reflow visually; source order never changes

## Composition

- Compose with **FormField** — FormLayout arranges the fields; each field keeps its own FormField wiring
  
  ```tsx
  <FormLayout layout="grid" columns={2}><FormField …>…</FormField></FormLayout>
  ```
- Compose with **Form** — Layouts live inside a Form (or standalone for filter bars)
- Compose with **Fieldset** — Fieldset when the legend/grouping IS the point; FormLayout when spacing/arrangement is
- Related: FormField, Form, Fieldset, Grid

---

# Grid / GridItem

Typed CSS grid with column counts per breakpoint (literal utilities that survive purging), auto-fit min-column mode, and GridItem spans.

> Import: `import { Grid } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/grid.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Grid layout should be declarative without stepping on Tailwind's compiler: column counts map to literal class names the scanner can see, and responsive card grids use minmax() auto-fit via minCol — no breakpoint math, no purged runtime-built classes. GridItem adds per-cell spans with the same literal approach.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cols | `number` | `auto (minCol) or browser default` | no | Base column count (1-6). |
| smCols | `number` | — | no | Columns from the sm breakpoint up (1-6). |
| mdCols | `number` | — | no | Columns from the md breakpoint up (1-6). |
| lgCols | `number` | — | no | Columns from the lg breakpoint up (1-6). |
| minCol | `string` | `undefined` | no | Auto-fit mode: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(<minCol>, 1fr)) — cards wrap responsively. Overrides the cols* props. |
| gap | `'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl'` | `md` | no | Token gap between cells. |
| as | `'div' | 'span' | 'section' | 'ul'` | — | no | Semantic element (use 'ul' with GridItem as="li" for item grids). |
| span | `number` | — | no | GridItem column span at the base breakpoint (1-6). |
| smSpan | `number` | — | no | GridItem column span from sm up (1-6). |
| mdSpan | `number` | — | no | GridItem column span from md up (1-6). |
| lgSpan | `number` | — | no | GridItem column span from lg up (1-6). |

## Examples

### Responsive card grid (auto-fit)

minmax() wrapping — works at every width without breakpoint columns.

```tsx
<Grid minCol="18rem" gap="lg">
  {cards.map((c) => (
    <Card key={c.id}>…</Card>
  ))}
</Grid>
```

### Fixed columns with a hero span

Literal grid-cols-*/col-span-* classes are compiled (they exist verbatim in source).

```tsx
<Grid cols={2} mdCols={3} gap="md">
  <GridItem span={2} mdSpan={2} className="…">Hero</GridItem>
  <GridItem>Card A</GridItem>
  <GridItem>Card B</GridItem>
</Grid>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't build column classes at runtime** — Template-built utilities (md:grid-cols-${n}) are invisible to Tailwind's scanner and get purged — the grid silently collapses to one column. The cols props use pre-declared literal classes.
- **Don't nest grids for one-axis layouts** — Row/column alignment is Flex's job; nesting grids adds template complexity with no benefit.

## Accessibility

- **Layout-only semantics**: Renders div/section/ul — no interactive behavior added
- **Reading order equals DOM order**: Visual column reflow never reorders DOM nodes

## Composition

- Compose with **Flex** — Flex for one-axis rows; Grid for two-axis layout
- Compose with **Card** — The classic minCol grid cell — cards wrap responsively
- Related: Flex, Card, Block

---

# Heading

Semantic heading (h1-h6) with a safe default scale and an optional visual-size override.

> Import: `import { Heading } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/heading.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Document structure and visual size are different axes: screen readers and SEO need the correct h-level, while design sometimes needs a smaller visual size. Heading takes level (semantic) and size (visual) separately so outline integrity never gets sacrificed for typography.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| level | `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` | — | yes | Semantic level — renders the matching h1..h6 element. |
| size | `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' | '3xl'` | — | no | Visual size override, independent of the semantic level. |
| muted | `boolean` | `false` | no | Use the muted-foreground token instead of the primary text color. |

## Examples

### Structural heading with visual override

```tsx
<Heading level={2}>Section title</Heading>

{/* h4 semantics (correct outline position) but large visual size) */}
<Heading level={4} size="2xl">Card headline</Heading>
```

### Muted subheading

```tsx
<Heading level={3} size="sm" muted>Supporting label</Heading>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Never skip levels for styling** — Jumping h1 -> h3 breaks the outline assistive tech announces. Use size for visual weight; level stays sequential.
- **Don't use Text as a heading** — A bolded paragraph is not a heading: navigation panes and find-in-page won't index it.

## Accessibility

- **Correct heading elements**: Renders h1..h6 from the level prop; default scale keeps visual hierarchy aligned with structure
- **Tokenized color**: muted uses --muted-foreground (AA in both themes)

## Composition

- Compose with **Text** — Headings introduce sections; Text carries the prose
- Related: Text, Block

---

# InlineCitation

Perplexity-style inline citation chip that reveals the source title and snippet on hover or keyboard focus.

> Import: `import { InlineCitation } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/inline-citation.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

Attribute individual claims inside a response to their source without leaving the paragraph.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| source | `SourceItem` | — | yes | Cited source powering the preview card. |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | no | Wrapped text; defaults to the source title. |

## Examples

### Wrap a claim

```tsx
<InlineCitation source={sources[0]}>as reported</InlineCitation>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not stack many citations on one word** — Use Sources footer for long lists; keep inline citations to one claim each.

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard access**: Trigger is a focusable button; card opens on focus-within.
- **Tooltip semantics**: Card has role=tooltip linked via aria-describedby.

---

# Input

A text input field with support for various input types and standard HTML input attributes

> Import: `import { Input } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/input.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

The Input component provides a styled text input that follows the design system. It supports all standard HTML input attributes and includes proper focus states, disabled states, and file input styling.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| type | `string` | `text` | no | HTML input type (text, password, email, number, etc.) |
| placeholder | `string` | — | no | Placeholder text to display when input is empty |
| value | `string` | — | no | Current value of the input (controlled component) |
| defaultValue | `string` | — | no | Default value for uncontrolled input |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disables the input |
| required | `boolean` | `false` | no | Marks the input as required for form validation |
| onChange | `(event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void` | — | no | Handler called when input value changes |
| onFocus | `(event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void` | — | no | Handler called when input is focused |
| onBlur | `(event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void` | — | no | Handler called when input loses focus |

## Examples

### Basic text input

Simple text input with placeholder

```tsx
<Input placeholder="Enter your name" />
```

### Email input

Input optimized for email addresses

```tsx
<Input type="email" placeholder="user@example.com" />
```

### Password input

Input that obscures text for passwords

```tsx
<Input type="password" placeholder="Enter password" />
```

### Controlled input

Input with controlled state

```tsx
<Input 
  value={value}
  onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}
  placeholder="Controlled input"
/>
```

### Disabled input

Input that cannot be interacted with

```tsx
<Input disabled placeholder="Disabled input" />
```

### File input

Input for file uploads with styled file button

```tsx
<Input type="file" />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Input for multi-line text** — Input is for single-line text. Use Textarea for multi-line content.
- **Don't ignore validation** — Provide visual feedback for validation errors
- **Don't use vague placeholders** — Placeholders should describe what input is expected

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard navigation**: Input is natively focusable and supports all keyboard input
- **Screen reader support**: Input type and placeholder are announced. Use aria-label or aria-labelledby for additional context
- **Form validation**: Supports HTML5 validation attributes (required, pattern, min, max)
- **Disabled state**: Disabled inputs are not focusable and screen readers announce as disabled

## Composition

- Compose with **Label** — Inputs should always have associated labels for accessibility
  
  ```tsx
  <Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label><Input id="email" />
  ```
- Compose with **Form** — Inputs are typically used within form components for validation and submission
  
  ```tsx
  Form groups multiple inputs together for validation
  ```
- Related: Textarea, Label, Form, Select

---

# InputGroup

Composite input shell with flush left/right addons (icons, units, buttons) behind one outer outline; the nested field sheds its own border so the group reads as a single control.

> Import: `import { InputGroup } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/input-group.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Search fields, URL/unit inputs, and inline actions need affixes that sit flush inside the field. InputGroup owns the combined border and focus ring (the outline doubles as the affordance) while addons stay visually part of the field: ghost addons keep the group background, muted addons paint a light gray, and nested inputs are stripped of their own chrome via descendant selectors.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| side | `'left' | 'right'` | `left` | no | Edge the addon hugs (flush against the group outline). |
| variant | `'ghost' | 'muted'` | `ghost` | no | Addon surface: ghost keeps the group background, muted paints a light gray. |

## Examples

### URL field with unit affixes

Muted affixes carry the fixed parts of the value; only the middle is editable.

```tsx
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupAddon side="left" variant="muted">https://</InputGroupAddon>
  <Input placeholder="example.com" />
  <InputGroupAddon side="right" variant="muted">.com</InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Search with icon and action button

Leading icon is decorative; the trailing button is the pseudo action indicator.

```tsx
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupAddon side="left" aria-hidden="true"><SearchIcon size={16} /></InputGroupAddon>
  <Input aria-label="Search" placeholder="Search issues…" />
  <InputGroupAddon side="right" variant="muted">
    <Button size="sm" variant="ghost">Go</Button>
  </InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Numeric input with currency suffix

The unit sits flush right; the outline communicates editability.

```tsx
<InputGroup>
  <Input aria-label="Amount" type="number" defaultValue="10" />
  <InputGroupAddon side="right" variant="muted">PLN</InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't give nested inputs their own border** — The group's outer border is the control outline. Inner borders create double lines and break the flush-addon look — strip them with the group (built in) or avoid nesting a bordered Input.
- **Don't nest interactive elements without labels** — Addon buttons live inside the field's focus-within region; they still need accessible names and must not steal the field's label association.

## Accessibility

- **Single focus stop**: Focus ring renders on the group via focus-within; nested inputs keep keyboard focus and their label association (htmlFor/id still targets the input)
- **Decorative affixes**: Purely decorative icons/text in addons should carry aria-hidden or the input's aria-label should include the unit
- **Disabled state**: Nested input's disabled styling applies; addons are independent — disable buttons inside them yourself

## Composition

- Compose with **Input / Textarea / Select** — The nested field is the editable region; InputGroup strips its border/ring automatically
  
  ```tsx
  <InputGroup><InputGroupAddon side="left">@</InputGroupAddon><Input /></InputGroup>
  ```
- Compose with **FormField** — Wrap the whole group when it needs a persistent label or error
  
  ```tsx
  <FormField label="Search"><InputGroup>…</InputGroup></FormField>
  ```
- Compose with **Button** — Buttons inside addons are the action affordance — ghost/variant='ghost' keeps the flush look
  
  ```tsx
  <InputGroupAddon side="right"><Button size="sm">Go</Button></InputGroupAddon>
  ```
- Related: Input, FormField, Search, Button

---

# Label

An accessible form label that associates with its control

> Import: `import { Label } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/label.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Label names a form control so screen readers announce the field name together with its value and state. Use htmlFor to associate, or wrap the control.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| htmlFor | `string` | — | no | The id of the control this label describes |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | yes | The label text |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Examples

### Label with input

Associated label and input

```tsx
<Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
<Input id="email" type="email" />
```

### Required field

Marking required fields explicitly

```tsx
<Label htmlFor="name">Name (required)</Label>
<Input id="name" required />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use placeholder as a label** — Placeholders disappear on input and are skipped by many screen readers.

## Accessibility

- **Programmatic association**: htmlFor/id pairing links the label to its control

## Composition

- Compose with **Input** — Every input should have a label
  
  ```tsx
  <Label htmlFor="e">Email</Label><Input id="e" />
  ```
- Related: Input, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, Radio

---

# Link

Inline link primitive with default/muted/underline/arrow/external variants, asChild router support and safe external handling.

> Import: `import { Link } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/link.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Every codebase re-implements inline links with inconsistent variants and unsafe target=_blank. Link centralizes the variants, keeps a real <a href> (SEO, modified clicks) and adds rel=noopener plus a screen-reader note for external URLs.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| href | `string` | — | no | Destination URL (pass through or via asChild). |
| variant | `'default' | 'muted' | 'underline' | 'arrow' | 'external'` | `default` | no | Visual style. |
| asChild | `boolean` | `false` | no | Render the child (router Link) with link styling. |
| external | `boolean` | — | no | Force external handling; absolute http(s) URLs are auto-detected, mailto/tel never open a new tab. |

## Examples

### Inline link

Internal links stay client-side; absolute URLs open safely in a new tab.

```tsx
<Link href="/docs">Read the docs</Link>
<Link href="https://github.com" variant="external">GitHub</Link>
```

### Router link

Preserves prefetch and modified-click behavior.

```tsx
<Link asChild variant="underline"><RouterLink href="/posts">Posts</RouterLink></Link>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Link for buttons** — Actions belong in Button; Link is for navigation.

## Accessibility

- **Real anchors**: Renders <a href> so middle-click/modified clicks work
- **External notice**: External links get rel=noopener noreferrer and a screen-reader note

## Composition

- Compose with **Card / List** — asChild makes whole-card links safe
  
  ```tsx
  <Card asChild><Link href="/post">…</Link></Card>
  ```
- Related: Button, Breadcrumb, Card

---

# LinkTabs

Route-driven navigation tabs that render real links and mark the current path with aria-current="page".

> Import: `import { LinkTabs } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/link-tabs.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Tabs switch client-side panels; LinkTabs navigates between routes. Settings, account, and app sub-navigation are URL-driven, so they need link semantics, prefix/exact matching, and a router-agnostic link component rather than a tablist.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| items | `LinkTabsItem[]` | — | yes | Tabs in display order. Each item has label, href, optional exact, icon, and disabled. |
| activeHref | `string` | — | no | Current pathname used to mark the active tab. |
| linkComponent | `React.ElementType` | — | no | Router link element (Inertia Link, Next Link, react-router Link). Defaults to an anchor. |
| variant | `'default' | 'underline' | 'rounded'` | `default` | no | Visual style of the tab strip. |
| size | `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` | `md` | no | Control density. |
| label | `string` | `Section` | no | Accessible name for the navigation landmark. |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply. |

## Examples

### Settings sub-navigation

The active item receives aria-current="page"; prefix matching keeps parent sections active on child routes.

```tsx
<LinkTabs
  items={[
    { label: 'Profile', href: '/settings/profile', exact: true },
    { label: 'Billing', href: '/settings/billing' },
  ]}
  activeHref={pathname}
  linkComponent={Link}
/>
```

### Underline strip

```tsx
<LinkTabs items={items} activeHref={pathname} variant="underline" />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Tabs for route navigation** — Tabs is a tablist for switching panels in place. Use LinkTabs when the URL changes; screen readers and browser history expect links.
- **Don't hardcode the active state** — Pass activeHref from the router; the component handles exact vs prefix matching.

## Accessibility

- **Navigation landmark**: Renders a nav with an accessible label (default "Section").
- **Current page**: The active link receives aria-current="page".
- **Keyboard**: Native links are tabbable and activate with Enter.
- **Disabled tabs**: Disabled items render as spans with aria-disabled and no link.

## Composition

- Compose with **PageHeader** — Place LinkTabs directly below the page header for section navigation.
- Related: Tabs, Breadcrumb, PageHeader, Link

---

# List / ListItem

Semantic list (ul/li) for rows of related items: settings, results, nav — with leading/trailing slots, selection, and pressable rows.

> Import: `import { List } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/list.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Row collections are lists, not tables or div stacks: screen readers announce item counts and navigate by item. List/ListItem keep that semantics while providing the layout vocabulary (slots, dividers, density, selection) that real product UIs need — and a pressable row wraps its content in a button so ul > li structure stays valid.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| divided | `boolean` | `false` | no | Hairline dividers between rows (List). |
| bordered | `boolean` | `false` | no | Card-like surface and border around the list (List). |
| size | `'default' | 'compact'` | `default` | no | Row density (List). |
| leading | `ReactNode` | — | no | Leading slot: icon, avatar, status dot, or checkbox (ListItem). |
| trailing | `ReactNode` | — | no | Trailing slot: chevron, badge, meta, or action (ListItem). |
| selected | `boolean` | `false` | no | Marks the row as the active/selected item (ListItem). |
| description | `string` | — | no | Secondary line under the main content (ListItem). |
| onClick | `() => void` | — | no | Makes the row pressable — content renders inside a full-width button so list semantics stay intact (ListItem). |

## Examples

### Settings rows with selection

selected highlights the active row; description adds a sub-line.

```tsx
<List bordered divided>
  <ListItem leading={<Icon />} trailing={<Badge>new</Badge>} selected>
    Notifications
  </ListItem>
  <ListItem leading={<Icon />} description="Weekly digest every Monday">
    Digest
  </ListItem>
</List>
```

### Pressable rows

onClick renders the row content inside a <button> — keyboard and screen-reader behavior come free.

```tsx
<List bordered>
  {threads.map((t) => (
    <ListItem key={t.id} onClick={() => open(t.id)} trailing={<Chevron />}>
      {t.title}
    </ListItem>
  ))}
</List>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use a table for non-tabular rows** — Tables imply column relationships. Rows of independent items are lists — assistive tech announces them as such.
- **Don't put onClick on the li itself** — Let ListItem wrap content in a button (which it does automatically) — a click handler on li breaks list semantics for screen readers.

## Accessibility

- **Native list structure**: Renders <ul>/<li>; screen readers announce item counts and per-item navigation
- **Pressable rows are buttons**: onClick rows wrap content in a full-width <button> with focus ring and disabled support
- **Selection is visual only**: selected uses aria-current-less styling; add aria-current on the row via props when it marks location

## Composition

- Compose with **Block** — Wrap a List in a Block section for titled groups
- Compose with **Badge / Avatar** — Common leading/trailing slot content
- Related: Table, Menu, Card

---

# Menu

Dropdown menu with keyboard navigation, typeahead, and ARIA menu semantics

> Import: `import { Menu } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/menu.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Menu presents a list of actions in a floating panel anchored to a trigger. Supports arrow-key navigation, Home/End, Escape to close, and destructive item styling.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| open | `boolean` | — | no | Controlled open state |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` | — | no | Called when the open state changes |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | yes | MenuTrigger and MenuContent children |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |
| destructive | `boolean` | `false` | no | Renders the item in a destructive style (MenuItem component) |
| asChild | `boolean` | `false` | no | Render the child element (e.g. an <a>) as the menu item (MenuItem). |

## Examples

### Link menu item

Navigation items keep menuitem semantics.

```tsx
<MenuItem asChild>
  <a href="/settings">Settings</a>
</MenuItem>
```

### Actions menu

Dropdown with labeled actions and a destructive item

```tsx
<Menu>
  <MenuTrigger>Options</MenuTrigger>
  <MenuContent>
    <MenuLabel>Actions</MenuLabel>
    <MenuItem>Profile</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Settings</MenuItem>
    <MenuSeparator />
    <MenuItem destructive>Sign out</MenuItem>
  </MenuContent>
</Menu>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Menu for navigation** — Menu is for actions. Use links or a navigation menu for page navigation.
- **Don't put forms inside a Menu** — Menus close on interaction. Use a Popover or Dialog for form inputs.

## Accessibility

- **Menu semantics**: role=menu on the panel, role=menuitem on items, aria-haspopup/aria-expanded on the trigger
- **Keyboard navigation**: Arrow keys move between items, Home/End jump to ends, Escape closes
- **Focus management**: Focus moves to items on arrow navigation and returns to trigger on close

## Composition

- Compose with **MenuTrigger** — Every Menu needs a MenuTrigger
  
  ```tsx
  <MenuTrigger>Options</MenuTrigger>
  ```
- Compose with **MenuItem** — Items are keyboard-navigable and close the menu on select
  
  ```tsx
  <MenuItem onClick={handleDelete} destructive>Delete</MenuItem>
  ```
- Related: Tooltip, Dialog

---

# Message

A chat message component that displays messages from users, assistants, or system prompts with optional avatars

> Import: `import { Message } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/message.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

The Message component renders individual chat messages with proper styling based on the message role (user, assistant, system, tool). It handles avatar display, timestamps, and different visual treatments to distinguish between message types in a conversation interface.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| message | `Message` | — | yes | The message object containing role, content, and optional metadata |
| showAvatar | `boolean` | `true` | no | Whether to show the avatar for the message |
| avatarSrc | `string` | — | no | Optional custom avatar image URL |
| avatarFallback | `string` | — | no | Fallback text to show when avatar image is not available |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply to the message container |
| renderContent | `(content: string) => ReactNode` | — | no | Custom renderer (e.g. markdown); replaces default plain-text rendering. |
| isStreaming | `boolean` | `false` | no | Shows a typing cursor and sets aria-busy while the response is still generating. |
| userLabel | `string` | `You` | no | Display name for user messages; enables localization. |
| assistantLabel | `string` | `Assistant` | no | Display name for assistant messages; enables localization. |
| error | `string` | — | no | Error text to render on the message; shows an error card with retry |
| onRetry | `() => void` | — | no | Called when the user requests a retry after error; omit to hide the action |
| labels | `{ retry?: string; edit?: string; save?: string; cancel?: string }` | — | no | Override button labels in the message actions |
| onEditContent | `(content: string) => void` | — | no | Enables edit-and-resubmit; called with the edited content |

## Examples

### User message

Message from the user with default avatar

```tsx
<Message message={{ id: '1', role: 'user', content: 'Hello, how are you?' }} />
```

### Assistant message

Message from the AI assistant

```tsx
<Message message={{ id: '2', role: 'assistant', content: 'I\'m doing well, thank you!' }} />
```

### System message

System-level message with distinct styling

```tsx
<Message message={{ id: '3', role: 'system', content: 'System initialized' }} />
```

### With custom avatar

Message with custom avatar image and fallback

```tsx
<Message 
  message={{ id: '4', role: 'assistant', content: 'Hello' }}
  avatarSrc="/ai-avatar.png"
  avatarFallback="AI"
/>
```

### Without avatar

Message with avatar hidden for more compact display

```tsx
<Message 
  message={{ id: '5', role: 'user', content: 'Quick message' }}
  showAvatar={false}
/>
```

### Markdown rendering (opt-in)

```tsx
<Message message={m} renderContent={(c) => <ReactMarkdown>{c}</ReactMarkdown>} />
```

### Streaming response

```tsx
<Message message={partial} isStreaming />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use for complex content** — Message content should be plain text. For complex UI, use additional components.
- **Don't hardcode message data** — Messages should come from a conversation state, not be hardcoded

## Accessibility

- **Screen reader support**: Message role and content are announced. Avatar has proper alt text from fallback or role
- **Color contrast**: User and assistant messages have distinct background colors with proper contrast
- **Semantic structure**: Message is rendered as a div with proper ARIA attributes for role identification

## Composition

- Compose with **Conversation** — Messages are typically rendered within a Conversation component that manages the message list
  
  ```tsx
  <Conversation>
  {messages.map(msg => <Message key={msg.id} message={msg} />)}
</Conversation>
  ```
- Compose with **PromptInput** — New messages from PromptInput should be added to the message list and rendered as Message components
  
  ```tsx
  const handleSubmit = (text) => {
  const newMessage = { id: Date.now(), role: 'user', content: text };
  setMessages([...messages, newMessage]);
}
  ```
- Related: Conversation, PromptInput, Avatar

---

# MessageActions

Feedback toolbar for an AI response: copy to clipboard, thumbs up/down rating, and regenerate. Every action is a callback; the component holds no conversation state.

> Import: `import { MessageActions } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/message-actions.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

Collect user trust signals (copy, rating, regeneration) with minimal API surface; consumers own what happens after each action.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| content | `string` | — | no | Text to copy; omit to hide the copy action. |
| onCopy | `(content: string) => void` | — | no | Called after copy with the copied text. |
| onFeedback | `(rating: 'up' | 'down' | undefined) => void` | — | no | Rating callback; selecting the active rating again passes undefined. |
| onRegenerate | `() => void` | — | no | Regeneration request; omit to hide the action. |
| autohide | `'always' | 'on-hover' | 'not-last'` | `always` | no | Controls visibility: always visible, visible on hover/focus, or hidden until hover for non-latest messages. |
| labels | `{ copy?, copied?, thumbUp?, thumbDown?, regenerate? }` | — | no | Overrides for all visible labels; enables localization. |

## Examples

### Full feedback bar

```tsx
<MessageActions content={message.content} onCopy={copy} onFeedback={(r) => track(r)} onRegenerate={regen} />
```

### Ratings only

```tsx
<MessageActions onFeedback={(r) => save(r)} />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not place MessageActions inside the message text flow** — Render it below the Message bubble so actions remain visually and semantically separate from content.

## Accessibility

- **Toolbar semantics**: Root has role=toolbar with an aria-label.
- **Toggle state**: Rating buttons expose aria-pressed so screen readers announce selection.
- **Icon buttons**: All icon-only controls have accessible labels; labels are localizable.

---

# MetricCard

KPI tile: label, value, directional delta (arrow + color) and supporting hint.

> Import: `import { MetricCard } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/metric-card.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Dashboards need comparable tiles. MetricCard standardizes tabular numbers, delta direction (never color-only) and the label/value/hint hierarchy so rows of KPIs align.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| label | `string` | — | yes | Metric name. |
| value | `string | number` | — | yes | Primary number/value; rendered tabular. |
| delta | `string` | — | no | Signed change, e.g. +12.4%. |
| trend | `'up' | 'down' | 'flat'` | `flat` | no | Delta direction color + arrow glyph. |
| hint | `React.ReactNode` | — | no | Comparison context (vs last month). |
| icon | `ReactNode` | — | no | Decorative icon. |

## Examples

### KPI row

Deltas carry arrows as well as color.

```tsx
<div className="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-3">
  <MetricCard label="Revenue" value="$12,480" delta="+12.4%" trend="up" hint="vs last month" />
  <MetricCard label="Churn" value="2.1%" delta="-0.4" trend="down" />
</div>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't encode meaning in color alone** — Always pass trend so the arrow glyph accompanies the color.

## Accessibility

- **Color-independent direction**: Delta renders ↑/↓/→ glyphs alongside color

## Composition

- Compose with **Grid** — Lay KPI rows out with Grid for even columns
  
  ```tsx
  <Grid columns={3} gap="md"><MetricCard … /></Grid>
  ```
- Related: Card, Grid, Progress

---

# PageHeader

Standard page heading: optional breadcrumbs, level-1 title, description, right-aligned actions and a sub-row slot.

> Import: `import { PageHeader } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/page-header.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Every list/detail page repeats breadcrumb + title + description + actions with drifting spacing. PageHeader fixes the hierarchy (one h1 per page) and the responsive wrap, so pages stay consistent.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| title | `string` | — | yes | Page heading rendered as h1. |
| description | `string` | — | no | Supporting summary under the title. |
| breadcrumbs | `ReactNode` | — | no | Trail rendered above the title. |
| actions | `ReactNode` | — | no | Right-aligned actions (buttons, menus). |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | no | Sub-row under the title (tabs, filters). |
| eyebrow | `ReactNode` | — | no | Kicker above the title. |
| size | `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'hero'` | `md` | no | Heading scale; hero is for marketing pages. |
| align | `'left' | 'center'` | `left` | no | Text alignment. |

## Examples

### List page header

One h1, one action cluster.

```tsx
<PageHeader
  title="Classes"
  description="Manage your weekly schedule."
  breadcrumbs={<Breadcrumb … />}
  actions={<Button>New class</Button>}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't stack multiple h1s** — PageHeader renders the page's h1; section headings inside the page should be h2 via Heading.

## Accessibility

- **Heading hierarchy**: Renders exactly one level-1 heading

## Composition

- Compose with **Breadcrumb** — Pass a Breadcrumb as breadcrumbs for hierarchy context
  
  ```tsx
  <PageHeader breadcrumbs={<Breadcrumb items={trail} />} title="Detail" />
  ```
- Related: Breadcrumb, Heading, Tabs

---

# Pagination

Numeric pagination with prev/next and boundary jumps; accepts page/pageCount or currentPage/totalPages and derives the count (plus a Showing X-Y of Z summary) from total/pageSize.

> Import: `import { Pagination } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/pagination.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Pagination lets users navigate through paged content. It shows page numbers with ellipsis for large ranges, prev/next buttons, and marks the current page with aria-current=page.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| page | `number` | `1` | no | Current page (1-based). Alias: currentPage. |
| pageCount | `number` | — | no | Total pages. Alias: totalPages, or derived from total/pageSize. |
| currentPage | `number` | — | no | Alias for page (migration-friendly). |
| totalPages | `number` | — | no | Alias for pageCount. |
| pageSize | `number` | — | no | Rows per page; with total enables the summary and derives pageCount. |
| total | `number` | — | no | Total item count for the summary. |
| itemLabel | `string` | `items` | no | Noun used in the summary. |
| showSummary | `boolean` | — | no | Force the summary on/off (defaults on when total and pageSize are set). |
| onPageChange | `(page: number) => void` | — | no | Called with the new page number. |
| siblings | `number` | `1` | no | Page buttons shown around the current page. |
| showBoundaries | `boolean` | `false` | no | Show first/last jump buttons. |
| showFirst | `boolean` | — | no | Force-show the first-page button. |
| showLast | `boolean` | — | no | Force-show the last-page button. |
| icons | `PaginationIcons` | — | no | Replace the default glyphs. |
| labels | `{ pagination?: string; first?: string; previous?: string; next?: string; last?: string; page?: (page: number) => string }` | — | no | Localized landmark and control labels. |

## Examples

### Summary + derived pages

Renders "Showing 26–50 of 312 students" and derives 13 pages.

```tsx
<Pagination
  page={page}
  pageSize={25}
  total={312}
  itemLabel="students"
  onPageChange={setPage}
/>
```

### Migration aliases

currentPage/totalPages map onto page/pageCount.

```tsx
<Pagination currentPage={page} totalPages={pages} onPageChange={setPage} />
```

### Basic pagination

Navigate through 10 pages

```tsx
<Pagination page={3} pageCount={10} onPageChange={setPage} />
```

### Wide page range

Show more page buttons around the current page

```tsx
<Pagination page={5} pageCount={20} siblings={2} onPageChange={setPage} />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Pagination for infinite scroll content** — Pagination implies discrete pages. Use a 'Load more' button or infinite scroll for continuous content.
- **Don't hide the current page number** — Users need to know where they are. Always show the active page with aria-current=page.

## Accessibility

- **Navigation landmark**: nav[aria-label=Pagination]
- **Current page**: Active button has aria-current=page
- **Disabled buttons**: Prev/next are disabled at the boundaries

## Composition

- Compose with **Table** — Paginate long table data
  
  ```tsx
  <Table>...</Table><Pagination page={page} pageCount={total} onPageChange={setPage} />
  ```
- Related: Table, Breadcrumb

---

# PasswordInput

Password field with an accessible show/hide toggle (aria-pressed), built on Input.

> Import: `import { PasswordInput } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/password-input.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Users mistype passwords; a reveal toggle reduces failed sign-ins. The toggle must be a real button with a pressed state and a proper label so it is not a mystery control.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| showLabel | `string` | `Show password` | no | Accessible label while hidden. |
| hideLabel | `string` | `Hide password` | no | Accessible label while visible. |

## Examples

### Sign-in field

Input props pass through.

```tsx
<PasswordInput aria-label="Password" autoComplete="current-password" />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't reveal by default** — Start masked; reveal is user-initiated.

## Accessibility

- **Toggle semantics**: Button with aria-pressed and Show/Hide labels

## Composition

- Compose with **FormField** — Wrap for label/hint/error wiring
  
  ```tsx
  <FormField id="pw" label="Password"><PasswordInput /></FormField>
  ```
- Related: Input, FormField, InputGroup

# Popover

Floating panel anchored to a trigger with interactive content, closing on outside click and Escape

> Import: `import { Popover } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/popover.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Popover displays interactive content (links, buttons, forms) in a floating panel. Unlike Tooltip, the content is focusable and actionable. Closes on outside click and Escape.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| open | `boolean` | — | no | Controlled open state |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` | — | no | Called when the open state changes |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | yes | PopoverTrigger and PopoverContent children |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Examples

### Simple popover

Popover with text and a button

```tsx
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger>Details</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent>
    <p>More information here.</p>
    <Button size="sm">Action</Button>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

### Controlled popover

Popover driven by parent state

```tsx
<Popover open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <PopoverTrigger>Options</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent>
    <form>...</form>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Popover for plain text hints** — Use Tooltip for non-interactive hints. Popover is for interactive content.
- **Don't use Popover for critical forms or destructive actions** — Popovers close on outside click, which can interrupt form filling. Use Dialog for forms and destructive confirmations.

## Accessibility

- **Dialog semantics**: role=dialog with aria-labelledby linking to the trigger
- **Escape dismissal**: Escape closes the popover

## Composition

- Compose with **PopoverTrigger** — Every Popover needs a PopoverTrigger
  
  ```tsx
  <PopoverTrigger>Open</PopoverTrigger>
  ```
- Related: Tooltip, Dialog, Menu

---

# Progress

A determinate progress bar with role=progressbar and exact value semantics

> Import: `import { Progress } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/progress.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Progress shows completion of a known-length task (uploads, installs, multi-step flows). It exposes exact values so assistive tech reports percentages, not just a moving bar.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| value | `number` | `0` | no | Current value between 0 and max |
| max | `number` | `100` | no | Upper bound of the progress scale |
| label | `string` | — | no | Accessible label announced by screen readers |
| indicatorClassName | `string` | — | no | Extra classes for the filled indicator (e.g. a semantic color). |
| indicatorStyle | `React.CSSProperties` | — | no | Inline styles for the filled indicator (e.g. a data-viz color). |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Examples

### Upload progress

Track an upload percentage

```tsx
<Progress value={uploadPercent} label="Upload progress" />
```

### Step completion

Progress through a finite set of steps

```tsx
<Progress value={step} max={totalSteps} label="Setup progress" />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Progress for indeterminate work** — When the duration is unknown, use Spinner or StreamingIndicator instead.
- **Don't animate progress beyond its value** — Fabricating movement misleads users; only reflect real task progress.

## Accessibility

- **Progressbar semantics**: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max
- **Exact values**: aria-valuenow reflects the clamped value

## Composition

- Compose with **Skeleton** — Use Skeleton for unknown-length content, Progress for known-length tasks
  
  ```tsx
  <Progress value={50} label="Upload" />
  ```
- Related: Skeleton, Spinner

---

# PromptInput

A textarea input for entering chat prompts with auto-resize, keyboard shortcuts, and send button

> Import: `import { PromptInput } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/prompt-input.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

The PromptInput component provides a specialized input for chat interfaces. It handles auto-resizing as the user types, supports Enter to submit (Shift+Enter for new line), and integrates with the conversation flow. It's designed to be the primary way users interact with AI assistants.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| onSubmit | `(value: string) => void` | — | yes | Callback when the user submits the prompt |
| placeholder | `string` | `Type your message...` | no | Placeholder text to display when input is empty |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | no | Whether the input is disabled |
| isLoading | `boolean` | `false` | no | Whether a submission is currently in progress |
| autoFocus | `boolean` | `false` | no | Whether to auto-focus the input on mount |
| maxLength | `number` | — | no | Maximum character count for the input |
| showSendButton | `boolean` | `true` | no | Whether to show the send button |
| sendButtonText | `string` | `Send` | no | Text or icon for the send button |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply to the container |
| onStop | `() => void` | — | no | While loading, the send button becomes a stop button that calls this handler. |
| stopButtonText | `string` | `Stop generating` | no | Accessible label for the stop button; enables localization. |
| attachments | `AttachmentItem[]` | — | no | Controlled attachment list shown as chips above the input |
| onRemoveAttachment | `(id: string) => void` | — | no | Called when the user removes an attachment chip |
| onAttachmentsChange | `(attachments: AttachmentItem[]) => void` | — | no | Called when files are added via drag-and-drop, paste, or picker |
| hasError | `boolean` | — | no | Styles the input in an error state (e.g. after a rejected file) |
| accept | `string` | — | no | MIME types accepted for attachments (e.g. "image/*") |
| multiple | `boolean` | — | no | Allow selecting multiple files |
| maxFiles | `number` | — | no | Maximum number of attachments allowed |
| maxFileSize | `number` | — | no | Maximum file size in bytes; rejects larger files |
| onAttachmentError | `(error: string) => void` | — | no | Called when an attachment is rejected (size, type, or count limit) |
| globalDrop | `boolean` | — | no | Enable drop-anywhere-on-page file acceptance |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | no | Custom content rendered inside the input row (e.g. tool buttons) |
| tooltip | `string | { content: ReactNode; shortcut?: string }` | — | no | Tooltip content for a toolbar button; optionally includes a keyboard shortcut hint (PromptInput.Button sub-component) |
| active | `boolean` | `false` | no | Toggles the active state on a toolbar button (PromptInput.Button sub-component) |

## Examples

### Basic prompt input

Simple prompt input with default configuration

```tsx
<PromptInput onSubmit={(value) => console.log(value)} />
```

### With custom placeholder

Prompt input with custom placeholder text

```tsx
<PromptInput 
  onSubmit={handleSubmit}
  placeholder="Ask me anything about coding..."
/>
```

### With auto-focus

Auto-focuses the input when component mounts

```tsx
<PromptInput 
  onSubmit={handleSubmit}
  autoFocus={true}
/>
```

### With character limit

Limits input to 500 characters

```tsx
<PromptInput 
  onSubmit={handleSubmit}
  maxLength={500}
/>
```

### Without send button

Hides the send button (user must press Enter)

```tsx
<PromptInput 
  onSubmit={handleSubmit}
  showSendButton={false}
/>
```

### With loading state

Shows loading state and disables while AI is responding

```tsx
<PromptInput 
  onSubmit={handleSubmit}
  isLoading={isGenerating}
  disabled={isGenerating}
/>
```

### Cancellable generation

```tsx
<PromptInput onSubmit={send} isLoading={loading} onStop={() => abortRef.current.abort()} />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use for non-chat input** — PromptInput is specifically for chat interactions, not general form input
- **Don't ignore Enter key behavior** — Users expect Enter to submit. If you change this, communicate it clearly
- **Don't validate after submission** — Disable the input when empty rather than validating in the handler

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard navigation**: Full keyboard support with Enter to submit, Shift+Enter for new line
- **Screen reader support**: Textarea has proper label and placeholder. Button state is announced
- **Form validation**: Button is disabled when input is empty, preventing invalid submissions
- **Auto-resize**: Textarea automatically grows with content up to max-height

## Composition

- Compose with **Conversation** — PromptInput is typically used below a Conversation component to add new messages
  
  ```tsx
  Conversation displays messages, PromptInput submits new ones to the same messages array
  ```
- Compose with **ChatLayout** — PromptInput is often part of a ChatLayout that combines Conversation and input
  
  ```tsx
  ChatLayout wraps Conversation and PromptInput in a complete chat interface
  ```
- Related: Conversation, ChatLayout, Button

---

# Prose

Self-contained long-form typography for rendered markdown/MDX: headings, links, lists, code, tables, quotes and figures.

> Import: `import { Prose } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/prose.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Content sites need consistent article typography without depending on the Tailwind typography plugin. Prose styles rendered HTML via child selectors, so any remark/MDX pipeline can drop output inside.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| size | `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` | `md` | no | Type scale for body and headings. |

## Examples

### Article body

Wrap MDX/remark output; keep Shiki/KaTeX as-is.

```tsx
<Prose size="md">
  {renderedMarkdown}
</Prose>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use prose for app UI** — Prose targets article content; forms and dashboards use Text/Heading.

## Accessibility

- **Heading anchors**: scroll-mt offsets headings under sticky headers

## Composition

- Compose with **TableOfContents** — Pair long articles with a TOC + useScrollSpy
  
  ```tsx
  <Prose>{content}</Prose><TableOfContents headings={headings} />
  ```
- Related: TableOfContents, Heading, Text, CodeBlock
