# Radio

Native radio buttons grouped for mutually exclusive choices, with an accessible fieldset/legend wrapper

> Import: `import { Radio } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/radio.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Radio lets users pick exactly one option from a visible set. RadioGroup provides the shared name and accessible legend so screen readers announce group context.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| value | `string` | — | yes | The value this item contributes to the group |
| label | `string` | — | no | Visible label rendered next to the radio |
| checked | `boolean` | — | no | Controlled checked state (on Radio) |
| onCheckedChange | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — | no | Fired when the user selects this radio (on Radio) |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disables the radio |
| title | `string` | — | no | Section heading (RadioCard component) |
| description | `string` | — | no | Supporting line under the title (RadioCard component) |
| rounded | `boolean` | `true` | no | Outer border radius on the section; false gives square corners (RadioCard component) |
| legend | `string` | — | no | Accessible group label; rendered as <legend> inside a fieldset (RadioGroup component) |
| onValueChange | `(value: string) => void` | — | no | Called with the newly selected value (RadioGroup component) |
| orientation | `'vertical' | 'horizontal'` | `vertical` | no | Stack options (default) or lay them out in a wrapping row (RadioGroup component) |
| error | `string` | — | no | Group-level validation message; announced via role=alert (RadioGroup component) |
| defaultValue | `string` | — | no | Initial selected value when uncontrolled (RadioGroup component) |

## Examples

### Radio group

Mutually exclusive plan selection

```tsx
<RadioGroup name="plan" legend="Choose a plan" defaultValue="free">
  <RadioGroupItem value="free" label="Free" />
  <RadioGroupItem value="pro" label="Pro" />
</RadioGroup>
```

### Controlled group

Group driven by parent state

```tsx
<RadioGroup
  name="plan"
  legend="Plan"
  value={plan}
  onValueChange={setPlan}
>
  <RadioGroupItem value="free" label="Free" />
  <RadioGroupItem value="pro" label="Pro" />
</RadioGroup>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Radio for multi-select** — Radio is single-choice. Use Checkbox when users can pick more than one option.
- **Don't render bare radios without a group** — Without RadioGroup there is no shared name or legend, so screen readers can't convey the grouping.

## Accessibility

- **Group semantics**: RadioGroup renders a fieldset with a legend so the group name is announced
- **Arrow-key navigation**: Native radio behavior: arrows move selection within the group

## Composition

- Compose with **RadioGroup** — Always wrap Radio/RadioGroupItem in a RadioGroup
  
  ```tsx
  <RadioGroup name="x" legend="Choose"><RadioGroupItem value="a" label="A" /></RadioGroup>
  ```
- Related: Checkbox, Select, Label

---

# Reasoning

A collapsible component for displaying AI reasoning steps and chain-of-thought processes

> Import: `import { Reasoning } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/reasoning.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

The Reasoning component displays the step-by-step thought process of an AI agent. It's collapsible to avoid cluttering the interface while still providing transparency into how the AI arrived at its conclusions.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| steps | `ReasoningStep[]` | — | yes | Array of reasoning steps to display |
| collapsible | `boolean` | `true` | no | Whether the reasoning can be collapsed/expanded |
| defaultExpanded | `boolean` | `false` | no | Whether the reasoning is expanded by default |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |
| duration | `number` | — | no | Elapsed reasoning time in seconds; renders a duration chip |
| isStreaming | `boolean` | — | no | Shows a streaming indicator while reasoning is in progress |
| labels | `{ title?: string; count?: (count: number) => string; thinking?: string; step?: (index: number) => string }` | — | no | Localized header, count and step labels. |

## Examples

### Basic reasoning

Collapsible reasoning with multiple steps

```tsx
<Reasoning 
  steps={[
    { id: '1', content: 'I need to analyze the user\'s request.' },
    { id: '2', content: 'The user wants to know about React components.' },
    { id: '3', content: 'I should provide a comprehensive answer.' }
  ]}
/>
```

### Expanded by default

Reasoning that shows steps immediately

```tsx
<Reasoning 
  steps={steps}
  defaultExpanded={true}
/>
```

### Non-collapsible

Reasoning that cannot be collapsed

```tsx
<Reasoning 
  steps={steps}
  collapsible={false}
/>
```

### With timestamps

Reasoning steps with timing information

```tsx
<Reasoning 
  steps={[
    { id: '1', content: 'Step 1', timestamp: new Date() },
    { id: '2', content: 'Step 2', timestamp: new Date() }
  ]}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't show reasoning for simple responses** — Reasoning is valuable for complex tasks but adds noise for simple responses.
- **Don't make steps too verbose** — Reasoning steps should be concise and focused on key decision points.
- **Don't show empty reasoning** — The component returns null for empty arrays, but it's better to not render it at all.

## Accessibility

- **Collapsible state**: Uses aria-expanded to communicate collapsible state to screen readers
- **Keyboard navigation**: Collapsible button is keyboard accessible with Enter/Space to toggle
- **Visual hierarchy**: Steps are numbered and visually distinct with clear hierarchy

## Composition

- Compose with **Message** — Reasoning is typically displayed before or within an assistant's message to show thought process
  
  ```tsx
  Message component can contain Reasoning to show the AI's thinking before the final response
  ```
- Compose with **ToolCall** — Reasoning often precedes tool calls to explain why a tool is being used
  
  ```tsx
  Reasoning explains the decision to use a tool, ToolCall shows the actual tool invocation
  ```
- Related: Message, ToolCall, Conversation

---

# Response

Streaming-optimized markdown renderer for AI responses with GFM support, streaming-safe repair of incomplete syntax, and highlighted code blocks with copy.

> Import: `import { Response } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/response.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

Render AI output as rich content without flicker or broken partial syntax while tokens arrive.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| children | `string` | — | yes | Markdown content to render. |
| parseIncompleteMarkdown | `boolean` | `true` | no | Close unclosed emphasis/inline-code/fences during streaming. |

## Examples

### Basic response

```tsx
<Response>{assistantMessage.content}</Response>
```

### Inside Message

```tsx
<Message message={m} renderContent={(c) => <Response>{c}</Response>} />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not use Response inside a code fence context** — Response is the top-level renderer; nested Response instances double-parse content.

## Accessibility

- **Semantic HTML**: Headings, lists and tables are real elements announced correctly.
- **Code blocks**: Routed through CodeBlock with accessible copy button.

# Search

Select-with-search: type to filter a full-width dropdown of options, or arrow through the full set from an empty query.

> Import: `import { Search } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/search.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

A native <select> cannot filter and a free text input cannot constrain. Search covers the middle: constrained choice with inline filtering, full combobox a11y (role=combobox/aria-activedescendant), and a listbox that portals with fixed positioning so scrollable containers never clip it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| options | `SearchOption[]` | — | yes | The full option set; filtered client-side as the user types. |
| defaultValue | `string` | — | no | Initially selected option value (display starts on its label). |
| onValueChange | `(value: string) => void` | — | no | Called with the selected option's value. |
| placeholder | `string` | `'Search…'` | no | Input placeholder while no query is typed. |
| emptyText | `string` | `'No matching results'` | no | Shown when no option matches the query. |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disables the input and the dropdown. |
| value | `string | null` | — | no | Controlled selected value; display follows it (null clears). |

## Examples

### Constrained pick from a list

Keyboard: ArrowDown opens, arrows move, Enter selects, Escape closes.

```tsx
<Search
  aria-label="Assign to"
  placeholder="Search people…"
  options={people}
  onValueChange={(value) => setAssignee(value)}
/>
```

### With descriptions and keywords

keywords widen matching without widening the visible label.

```tsx
const options = [
  { value: 'a1', label: 'Ada Lovelace', description: 'Design', keywords: 'ada design ui' },
  { value: 'a2', label: 'Alan Turing', description: 'Platform', keywords: 'alan platform' },
];
<Search options={options} onValueChange={select} />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Search for free-form input** — Search constrains the result to known options. For values the system has never seen (tags, new names) use Input or Autocomplete instead.
- **Don't feed hundreds of options without keywords** — The list is filtered client-side; large sets need keywords/descriptions so short queries hit. For server-side search, debounce the query and swap the options prop — do not render raw HTML in labels.
- **Don't rely on the placeholder as the field's name** — The placeholder disappears once typing starts. Pass aria-label (standalone) or wrap the Search in FormField for a persistent accessible name.

## Accessibility

- **Combobox pattern**: Input exposes role=combobox with aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-autocomplete=list, and aria-activedescendant pointing at the active option
- **Keyboard operation**: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the active option (wrapping), Home/End jump, Enter selects, Escape closes without clearing
- **Focus retention**: Option mousedown is prevented so focus stays in the input while clicking; typing continues immediately after selection
- **Clipping-safe listbox**: The listbox portals to document.body with fixed coordinates measured from the input and closes on scroll/resize

## Composition

- Compose with **FormField** — Wrap in FormField when the search sits in a form — the label is cloned onto the input
  
  ```tsx
  <FormField id="assignee" label="Assign to"><Search options={people} /></FormField>
  ```
- Compose with **Autocomplete** — Choose Search for constrained picks; Autocomplete when free-form values must stay allowed
- Related: Autocomplete, Select, FormField, CommandPalette

---

# SectionHeading

Section heading block: eyebrow, title (level 2-4), description and actions, with left/center alignment and three sizes.

> Import: `import { SectionHeading } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/section-heading.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Marketing and content pages repeat the same eyebrow/title/description/actions cluster for every section. SectionHeading standardizes it without claiming the page h1 (that is PageHeader's job).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| title | `string` | — | yes | Section title. |
| description | `string` | — | no | Supporting copy. |
| eyebrow | `ReactNode` | — | no | Kicker above the title. |
| actions | `ReactNode` | — | no | Right-aligned actions. |
| level | `2 | 3 | 4` | `2` | no | Heading level rendered for the title. |
| align | `'left' | 'center'` | `left` | no | Text and action alignment. |
| size | `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` | `md` | no | Title scale. |

## Examples

### Marketing section

Eyebrow + title + copy + action link.

```tsx
<SectionHeading
  eyebrow="Components"
  title="Built for agents"
  description="Every component ships a spec."
  actions={<Link href="/docs">All docs</Link>}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use it for the page title** — PageHeader owns the single h1; SectionHeading defaults to h2.

## Accessibility

- **Configurable heading level**: Renders h2/h3/h4 via the level prop

## Composition

- Compose with **PageHeader** — PageHeader for the h1; SectionHeading for h2+ sections
  
  ```tsx
  <PageHeader title="…" /><SectionHeading title="…" />
  ```
- Related: PageHeader, Heading, Text

---

# Select

Accessible select built on the native <select> with flat options, optgroups, a placeholder row and native multi-select.

> Import: `import { Select } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/select.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Native selects keep platform keyboard, mobile picker and screen-reader behavior for free. Groups cover coarse categorization, placeholder renders the 'choose one' affordance, and multiple switches the contract to string[] for tag-picker use cases without reimplementing a listbox.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| options | `SelectOption[]` | — | no | Flat options ({ value, label, disabled? }). Ignored when groups is provided. |
| label | `string` | — | no | Visible label rendered and associated via htmlFor/aria |
| value | `string | string[]` | — | no | Controlled value (string, or string[] when multiple). |
| defaultValue | `string | string[]` | — | no | Initial value when uncontrolled. |
| onChange | `React.ChangeEventHandler<HTMLSelectElement>` | — | no | Native change event, compatible with react-hook-form register(). |
| groups | `SelectOptionGroup[]` | — | no | Optgroups: [{ label, options }] rendered with a heading per section. |
| placeholder | `string` | — | no | Renders a disabled empty option as the 'choose one' affordance. |
| multiple | `boolean` | `false` | no | Native multi-select; value/defaultValue and onValueChange switch to string[]. |
| onValueChange | `(value: string | string[]) => void` | — | no | Value-based callback for controlled usage; string[] when multiple. |

## Examples

### Grouped options

Optgroups with a placeholder row.

```tsx
<Select
  label="Plan"
  placeholder="Choose a plan"
  groups={[
    { label: 'Individual', options: [{ value: 'free', label: 'Free' }] },
    { label: 'Business', options: [{ value: 'team', label: 'Team' }] },
  ]}
/>
```

### Multi-select

Native listbox with a string[] contract.

```tsx
<Select
  label="Channels"
  multiple
  value={channels}
  onValueChange={setChannels}
  options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'slack', label: 'Slack' }]}
/>
```

### Controlled select

Keep the selected value in state and render it back through value.

```tsx
const [size, setSize] = useState('default');

<Select
  label="Size"
  value={size}
  onValueChange={setSize}
  options={[
    { value: 'default', label: 'Default' },
    { value: 'sm', label: 'Small' },
    { value: 'lg', label: 'Large' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not build a custom listbox for simple choices** — Hand-rolled listboxes rarely match native keyboard and screen-reader behavior. Use Select for flat option lists; consider CommandPalette for searchable command surfaces.

## Accessibility

- **Label association**: A visible label is connected with htmlFor/id; without one, aria-label is forwarded to the native select.
- **Platform keyboard and screen-reader support**: Built on the native select element, inheriting its full support matrix.

## Composition

- Compose with **Button** — Pair Select with Button in filter toolbars; Button submits, Select filters.
- Related: Button, Input

---

# SelectMenu

Custom listbox select for rich options: descriptions, icons, groups, multi-select, custom rows and hidden inputs for forms.

> Import: `import { SelectMenu } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/select-menu.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Native <select> cannot render rich option content. SelectMenu supplies a real listbox with the button/listbox keyboard model while keeping the same value/onValueChange contract as Select, so teams can move between the two without rewriting state.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| items | `SelectMenuItem[]` | — | yes | Options: { value, label, description?, icon?, disabled?, group? }. |
| value | `string | string[]` | — | no | Controlled value(s); string[] when multiple. |
| defaultValue | `string | string[]` | — | no | Initial value(s) when uncontrolled. |
| onValueChange | `(value: string | string[]) => void` | — | no | Fired with the new selection. |
| multiple | `boolean` | `false` | no | Allow several selections; the listbox stays open. |
| placeholder | `string` | `Select…` | no | Shown when nothing is selected. |
| name | `string` | — | no | Renders hidden form inputs for the selected values. |
| renderValue | `(selected: SelectMenuItem[]) => ReactNode` | — | no | Custom trigger content. |
| renderItem | `(item, state: { selected: boolean; active: boolean }) => ReactNode` | — | no | Custom option row. |
| emptyText | `string` | `No options` | no | Shown when items is empty. |

## Examples

### Rich options

Descriptions and grouped headings inside a real listbox.

```tsx
<SelectMenu
  aria-label="Plan"
  placeholder="Choose a plan"
  items={[
    { value: 'free', label: 'Free', description: '1 project', group: 'Individual' },
    { value: 'team', label: 'Team', description: 'SSO + audit log', group: 'Business' },
  ]}
  value={plan}
  onValueChange={setPlan}
/>
```

### Multi-select with form input

Hidden inputs make the selection submit with the form.

```tsx
<SelectMenu
  aria-label="Channels"
  multiple
  name="channels"
  items={channels}
  value={selected}
  onValueChange={setSelected}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use it for free-text entry** — SelectMenu has no text input. Use Autocomplete when typing a value is expected.
- **Don't render more than ~50 options** — There is no filtering. Large sets need Autocomplete or a searchable flow.

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard model**: Arrows move the active option, Home/End jump, Enter/Space select, Escape closes, typeahead jumps by first letters

## Composition

- Compose with **FormField** — Wrap for label/hint/error wiring
  
  ```tsx
  <FormField id="plan" label="Plan"><SelectMenu items={items} /></FormField>
  ```
- Compose with **Select** — Prefer Select when options are plain text (native pickers, mobile UX)
  
  ```tsx
  <Select options={plain} />
  ```
- Related: Select, Autocomplete, Menu, FormField

---

# Separator

A visual divider between content blocks, decorative or semantic

> Import: `import { Separator } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/separator.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Separator creates visual rhythm between content groups. By default it is decorative; pass a label to make it a semantic divider that assistive tech can announce.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| orientation | `'horizontal' | 'vertical'` | `horizontal` | no | Direction of the divider line |
| label | `string` | — | no | Accessible name; when set, the separator becomes semantic |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Examples

### Horizontal divider

Simple line between sections

```tsx
<div>Section A</div>
<Separator className="my-4" />
<div>Section B</div>
```

### Vertical divider

Vertical line between actions

```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-4">
  <Button>Save</Button>
  <Separator orientation="vertical" className="h-6" />
  <Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>
</div>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Separator to create layout spacing** — Use margin/gap for spacing; Separator is for visual division.

## Accessibility

- **Decorative by default**: role="none" so screen readers skip unlabeled separators
- **Semantic separator**: role="separator" with aria-label when labelled

## Composition

- Compose with **Section headings** — Separators pair with headings to divide long pages
  
  ```tsx
  <h2>Settings</h2><Separator className="my-4" />
  ```
- Related: Skeleton

---

# SiteFooter

Marketing footer: brand + tagline column, link columns and a legal bar; router-agnostic via linkComponent.

> Import: `import { SiteFooter } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/site-footer.json
> Tier: organism · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Footers are copied between projects with inconsistent link handling. SiteFooter provides the standard multi-column layout, safe external links and a legal row.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| brand | `ReactNode` | — | no | Brand slot. |
| tagline | `string` | — | no | Short line under the brand. |
| columns | `SiteFooterColumn[]` | — | yes | Link columns: { title, links: { label, href, external? }[] }. |
| legal | `ReactNode` | — | no | Bottom bar (copyright, legal links). |
| linkComponent | `React.ElementType` | — | no | Router link element. |

## Examples

### Standard footer

Brand, columns and legal row.

```tsx
<SiteFooter
  brand={<img src="/logo.svg" alt="Acme" className="h-10" />}
  tagline="Ship UI your AI understands."
  columns={[{ title: 'Docs', links: [{ label: 'Intro', href: '/docs' }] }]}
  legal={<span>© 2026 Acme</span>}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't duplicate the same links in two columns** — Keep each destination in exactly one column for predictable scanning.

## Accessibility

- **Landmark semantics**: Renders <footer> with headed link groups

## Composition

- Compose with **SiteHeader** — Pair for a complete marketing shell
  
  ```tsx
  <SiteHeader … />…<SiteFooter … />
  ```
- Related: SiteHeader, Link, Separator

# SiteHeader

Marketing/site header: sticky bar with brand, horizontal navigation with prefix-aware active states, right-aligned actions and a mobile drawer.

> Import: `import { SiteHeader } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/site-header.json
> Tier: organism · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Marketing sites repeat brand/nav/actions/mobile-menu wiring with custom active matching. SiteHeader standardizes the bar, handles /docs matching /docs/components, and stays router-agnostic via linkComponent.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| brand | `ReactNode` | — | yes | Brand slot (logo/lockup), wrapped in a link to /. |
| items | `SiteNavItem[]` | — | yes | Primary nav: { href, label, external? }. |
| activeHref | `string` | — | no | Current route for active styling (aria-current=page). |
| match | `'prefix' | 'exact'` | `prefix` | no | Prefix highlights parents of the current route; exact only identical hrefs. |
| actions | `ReactNode` | — | no | Right-aligned actions (theme toggle, GitHub, CTA). |
| linkComponent | `React.ElementType` | — | no | Router link element. |
| sticky | `boolean` | `true` | no | Pin the bar to the top. |
| mobileLabel | `string` | `Menu` | no | Title of the mobile navigation drawer. |

## Examples

### Marketing header

Prefix-active nav with a mobile drawer.

```tsx
<SiteHeader
  brand={<img src="/logo.svg" alt="Acme" className="h-8" />}
  items={[{ href: '/docs', label: 'Docs' }, { href: '/pricing', label: 'Pricing' }]}
  activeHref={pathname}
  linkComponent={RouterLink}
  actions={<ThemeToggle />}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use it for admin rails** — Vertical app navigation belongs in Sidebar + AppShell.

## Accessibility

- **Current page**: aria-current=page on the active link (prefix or exact matching)
- **Mobile navigation**: Burger opens a focus-trapped Drawer with the same items

## Composition

- Compose with **SiteFooter** — Pair header and footer for a complete marketing shell
  
  ```tsx
  <SiteHeader … /><main /><SiteFooter … />
  ```
- Compose with **Drawer** — The mobile menu is a Drawer automatically
  
  ```tsx
  <SiteHeader … />
  ```
- Related: SiteFooter, AppShell, Sidebar, Link

---

# Skeleton

A loading placeholder that mirrors the shape of upcoming content

> Import: `import { Skeleton } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/skeleton.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Skeleton reduces perceived loading time by showing the layout shape before data arrives. It is aria-hidden so screen readers skip it; pair with a live-region status to announce loading.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| className | `string` | — | no | Shape and size classes (e.g. h-4 w-32, rounded-full) |
| height | `string` | — | no | Tailwind height class for the block (e.g. 'h-4'). |
| width | `string` | `w-full` | no | Tailwind width class for the block (e.g. 'w-48'). |
| rounded | `'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'full'` | `md` | no | Corner preset — full for avatars/dots, none for tables. |

## Examples

### Text placeholder

Placeholder for a line of text

```tsx
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-32" />
```

### Card placeholder

Placeholder matching a card layout

```tsx
<div className="space-y-2">
  <Skeleton className="h-24 w-full rounded-lg" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-2/3" />
</div>
```

### With live-region announcement

Announcing the loading state to screen readers

```tsx
<span role="status" className="sr-only">Loading…</span>
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-48" />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Skeleton as a permanent element** — Skeletons are for loading states only; remove once content renders.
- **Don't use Skeleton without announcing loading** — Skeleton is aria-hidden. Add a role=status element so screen-reader users know something is loading.

## Accessibility

- **Hidden from assistive tech**: aria-hidden="true" on the placeholder
- **Reduced motion**: Pulse animation is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion

## Composition

- Compose with **Status region** — Always pair with a status region to announce loading
  
  ```tsx
  <span role="status" className="sr-only">Loading…</span><Skeleton className="h-4 w-32" />
  ```
- Related: Progress, Spinner

---

# Source / Sources

Displays citations and references for an AI response. `Source` renders a single citation; `Sources` renders a numbered list with an overflow count.

> Import: `import { Source } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/source.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

Make generated answers transparent by showing where information came from.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| index | `number` | — | no | 1-based citation marker rendered as [n]; omit on Source to hide numbering. |
| source | `SourceItem` | — | yes | The single source to render (Source component) |
| onSelect | `(source: SourceItem) => void` | — | no | Called when the source chip is clicked |
| sources | `SourceItem[]` | — | yes | List of sources to render (Sources component) |
| maxDisplay | `number` | `3` | no | Maximum number of source chips to show before collapsing (Sources component) |
| label | `string` | `Sources` | no | Section label above the source list (Sources component) |

## Examples

### Citations list

```tsx
<Sources sources={[{ id: '1', title: 'React docs', url: 'https://react.dev' }, { id: '2', title: 'MDN', url: 'https://developer.mozilla.org' }]} />
```

### Single inline citation

```tsx
<Source source={{ id: '1', title: 'React docs', url: 'https://react.dev' }} index={1} />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not nest Sources inside Sources** — Sources is a list container; compose individual Source items only when building a custom layout.

## Accessibility

- **Link semantics**: References use native links with rel=noopener when URLs are provided.
- **Decorative markers**: [n] citation markers are aria-hidden; titles are read as link text.

---

# Spinner

Indeterminate loading indicator with accessible status semantics.

> Import: `import { Spinner } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/spinner.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Communicate in-progress states without layout shift; inherit text color so it adapts to any context.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| size | `'sm' | 'default' | 'lg'` | `default` | no | Visual size of the spinner. |
| label | `string` | `Loading...` | no | Screen-reader label; the visual ring is aria-hidden. |

## Examples

### Default

```tsx
<Spinner />
```

### Inline loading state

```tsx
<span className="flex items-center gap-2"><Spinner size="sm" /> Generating...</span>
```

### Decorative (near visible text)

```tsx
<Spinner aria-hidden label="" />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not use multiple spinners for one wait state** — One status indicator per operation; multiple role=status elements announce redundantly.

## Accessibility

- **Status semantics**: role=status with sr-only label announces loading to screen readers.
- **Reduced motion**: Pair with motion-reduce utilities when animation must be suppressed.

# Stepper

Multi-step flow indicator: ordered list, aria-current step, text state for complete/current/upcoming.

> Import: `import { Stepper } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/stepper.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Wizards need orientation: where am I, what is done, what is next. A stepper built on an ordered list keeps the sequence structural and announces state in text, not just color.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| steps | `{ label: string; description?: string }[]` | — | yes | Ordered step definitions. |
| current | `number` | — | yes | Zero-based index of the active step. |
| orientation | `'horizontal' | 'vertical'` | `horizontal` | no | Layout direction. |
| onStepClick | `(index: number) => void` | — | no | Makes steps clickable (for revisit flows). |

## Examples

### Onboarding wizard

Current step is announced; completed steps show a check.

```tsx
<Stepper
  current={step}
  steps={[{ label: 'Account' }, { label: 'Studio details' }, { label: 'Invite team' }, { label: 'Review' }]}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use it for progress percentage** — Use Progress for measurable 0-100 progress; Stepper is discrete stages.

## Accessibility

- **Sequence + state**: Ordered list with aria-current=step and sr-only state text

## Composition

- Compose with **Form** — One Form (or Form step) per Stepper stage
  
  ```tsx
  <Stepper current={1} steps={steps} />
  ```
- Related: Progress, Tabs, Form

# Switch

A toggle switch for binary settings, with role=switch and aria-checked

> Import: `import { Switch } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/switch.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Switch represents an on/off setting that takes effect immediately. Unlike Checkbox, it signals a change of state rather than a form submission value.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| checked | `boolean` | — | no | Controlled on/off state |
| defaultChecked | `boolean` | — | no | Initial state when uncontrolled |
| onCheckedChange | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — | no | Fired when the user toggles the switch |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disables the switch |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Examples

### Settings toggle

Toggle in a settings row

```tsx
<div className="flex items-center justify-between">
  <Label htmlFor="notifications">Email notifications</Label>
  <Switch id="notifications" onCheckedChange={setEmails} />
</div>
```

### Controlled switch

Switch driven by parent state

```tsx
<Switch checked={dark} onCheckedChange={setDark} aria-label="Dark mode" />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Switch inside forms that need a submit** — Switch applies immediately. Use Checkbox when the value is submitted with a form.
- **Don't rely on color alone** — Switch position conveys state; keep the thumb contrast high in both themes.

## Accessibility

- **Switch semantics**: role="switch" with aria-checked announces on/off state
- **Keyboard toggle**: Space and Enter toggle the switch

## Composition

- Compose with **Label** — Pair with Label or aria-label
  
  ```tsx
  <Label htmlFor="s">Auto-save</Label><Switch id="s" />
  ```
- Related: Checkbox, Label

---

# Table

Semantic data table with headers, body, footer, and accessible caption

> Import: `import { Table } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/table.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Table displays tabular data with proper semantics. TableHead uses scope=col, TableCaption provides an accessible summary, and rows support hover/selected states.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| children | `ReactNode` | — | yes | TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter, and TableCaption children |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Examples

### Basic table

Table with caption, headers, and data rows

```tsx
<Table>
  <TableCaption>Monthly revenue</TableCaption>
  <TableHeader>
    <TableRow>
      <TableHead scope="col">Month</TableHead>
      <TableHead scope="col">Amount</TableHead>
    </TableRow>
  </TableHeader>
  <TableBody>
    <TableRow>
      <TableCell>January</TableCell>
      <TableCell>$1,200</TableCell>
    </TableRow>
  </TableBody>
</Table>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Table for layout** — Tables are for tabular data. Use CSS Grid or Flexbox for page layout.
- **Don't omit the caption** — Screen readers use the caption to describe the table's purpose.

## Accessibility

- **Semantic table**: Native table/thead/tbody/tfoot with scope attributes on headers
- **Accessible caption**: TableCaption describes the table contents

## Composition

- Compose with **TableHeader** — Place column headers in a TableHeader with TableRow
  
  ```tsx
  <TableHeader><TableRow><TableHead scope="col">Name</TableHead></TableRow></TableHeader>
  ```
- Related: Card, Badge

---

# TableCard

Table shell with title/description, header actions, optional toolbar, edge-to-edge body and a footer row.

> Import: `import { TableCard } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/table-card.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Every list page rebuilds the same chrome around Table/DataTable: heading, count, actions, filter row, pagination. TableCard standardizes that shell so pages only supply the table.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| title | `string` | — | no | Card heading. |
| description | `string` | — | no | Supporting line under the heading. |
| actions | `ReactNode` | — | no | Right-aligned header actions. |
| toolbar | `ReactNode` | — | no | Row between header and table (filters, bulk actions). |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | yes | Table or DataTable content. |
| footer | `ReactNode` | — | no | Footer row (pagination, summary). |
| flush | `boolean` | `true` | no | Remove inner padding so the table reaches the card edges. |

## Examples

### List page table

Header, toolbar, table and pagination in one surface.

```tsx
<TableCard
  title="Classes"
  description="12 active"
  actions={<Button>New class</Button>}
  toolbar={<FilterBar … />}
  footer={<Pagination … />}
>
  <DataTable columns={columns} data={rows} />
</TableCard>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't nest another bordered card** — TableCard is the surface; wrapping it in Card double-borders the content.

## Accessibility

- **Heading semantics**: Title renders an h2 (page owns the h1 via PageHeader)
- **Table labelling**: The table keeps its own caption/aria-label

## Composition

- Compose with **DataTable** — Body content; use flush for edge-to-edge rows
  
  ```tsx
  <TableCard flush><DataTable … /></TableCard>
  ```
- Compose with **FilterBar** — Pass as toolbar for list filtering
  
  ```tsx
  <TableCard toolbar={<FilterBar … />}>…</TableCard>
  ```
- Compose with **Pagination** — Pass as footer
  
  ```tsx
  <TableCard footer={<Pagination … />}>…</TableCard>
  ```
- Related: DataTable, Table, FilterBar, Pagination, Card

---

# TableOfContents

Sticky 'On this page' navigation with nested levels and aria-current, plus a useScrollSpy hook for the active heading.

> Import: `import { TableOfContents } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/table-of-contents.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Long-form pages drift into bespoke TOC implementations. TableOfContents fixes the nested list, active styling and landmark name; useScrollSpy supplies the active id from real scroll position.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| headings | `TocHeading[]` | — | yes | Headings: { id, text, level: 2 | 3 | 4 }. |
| activeId | `string` | — | no | Controlled active heading (pair with useScrollSpy). |
| label | `string` | `On this page` | no | Accessible name of the nav landmark. |
| sticky | `boolean` | `true` | no | Stick while the article scrolls. |

## Examples

### Article TOC

Scroll-spy driven active state.

```tsx
const activeId = useScrollSpy(headings.map((h) => h.id));

<TableOfContents headings={headings} activeId={activeId} />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't hardcode the active id** — Compute it from scroll position so the highlight follows the reader.

## Accessibility

- **Landmark + current item**: nav aria-label plus aria-current=location on the active link

## Composition

- Compose with **Prose** — Pairs with article bodies
  
  ```tsx
  <TableOfContents headings={headings} activeId={active} />
  ```
- Related: Prose, Breadcrumb, List

---

# Tabs

Tabbed content container with ARIA tablist semantics and keyboard navigation

> Import: `import { Tabs } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/tabs.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Tabs organize related content into switchable panels. Tabs manages the active tab, wires ARIA relationships, and uses roving tabindex so keyboard users move through tabs with arrow keys.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| value | `string` | — | no | Controlled active tab value |
| defaultValue | `string` | — | no | Initial tab value when uncontrolled |
| onValueChange | `(value: string) => void` | — | no | Called when the active tab changes |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | yes | TabsList, TabsTrigger, and TabsContent children |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |
| variant | `'default' | 'underline' | 'rounded'` | `default` | no | Strip design: enclosed pill track (default), background-free underline, or fully-rounded pill track. |
| size | `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` | `md` | no | Density for the strip and its triggers. |

## Examples

### Basic tabs

Two-tab layout with panels

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="analytics">Analytics</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="overview">Overview panel</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="analytics">Analytics panel</TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

### Controlled tabs

Tabs driven by parent state

```tsx
<Tabs value={tab} onValueChange={setTab}>
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value="one">One</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="two">Two</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="one">Panel one</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="two">Panel two</TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Tabs for primary navigation** — Tabs switch content within a view. Use links or a navigation menu for moving between pages.
- **Don't nest Tabs more than one level deep** — Nested tabs disorient users; use sections or accordions instead.

## Accessibility

- **Tablist semantics**: role=tablist/tab/tabpanel with aria-selected and aria-controls
- **Roving tabindex**: Only the active tab is tabbable; arrow keys move between tabs

## Composition

- Compose with **TabsList** — Wrap triggers in a TabsList for correct semantics
  
  ```tsx
  <TabsList><TabsTrigger value="a">A</TabsTrigger></TabsList>
  ```
- Related: Separator, Button

---

# Text

Semantic paragraph text with a controlled type scale; renders a real p (or span with inline).

> Import: `import { Text } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/text.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Body copy should be a paragraph element, not a styled div — reader modes, screen readers, and document outline all depend on semantics. Text gives you the type scale, weight, and muted tone as typed props so spacing and color stay tokenized instead of ad-hoc utilities.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| inline | `boolean` | `false` | no | Render as an inline span instead of a block p (the inline-block variation). |
| size | `'xs' | 'sm' | 'base' | 'lg' | 'xl'` | `base` | no | Type scale step. |
| weight | `'normal' | 'medium' | 'semibold' | 'bold'` | — | no | Font weight. |
| muted | `boolean` | `false` | no | Use the muted-foreground token instead of the primary text color. |

## Examples

### Paragraph and inline text

block by default; inline for span-level flow.

```tsx
<Text>Default body paragraph.</Text>
<Text size="sm" muted>Secondary helper copy.</Text>
<Text weight="semibold">Emphasized lead-in.</Text>

{/* Inline flow — renders a <span> */}
<Text inline size="sm">Read the </Text>
<Link href="/docs">docs</Link>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use divs for copy** — A div with text classes is invisible to document outline, reader mode, and search extraction. Use Text (p) for paragraphs and Heading for titles.
- **Don't skip headings for visual size** — Pick the Heading LEVEL that matches the document structure and use size for visual override — never a large Text.

## Accessibility

- **Real text elements**: Renders <p>/<span>, so assistive tech and reader modes treat content as text
- **Muted tone is tokenized**: muted uses --muted-foreground, which meets AA in both themes

## Composition

- Compose with **Heading** — Headings structure the document; Text carries the prose between them
- Compose with **Block** — Use Block (div) for layout wrappers around Text, not instead of it
- Related: Heading, Block

---

# Textarea

A multi-line text input styled to match Input, wrapping the native textarea

> Import: `import { Textarea } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/textarea.json
> Tier: atom · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Textarea is for free-form, multi-line text such as messages, descriptions, and feedback. Native textarea semantics keep IME, form validation, and screen-reader behavior intact.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| value | `string` | — | no | Controlled value; omit for uncontrolled usage |
| defaultValue | `string` | — | no | Initial value when uncontrolled |
| placeholder | `string` | — | no | Placeholder text shown when empty |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | no | Disables the textarea |
| onChange | `(event: ChangeEvent<HTMLTextAreaElement>) => void` | — | no | Fired when the content changes |

## Examples

### Basic textarea

Multi-line input with a placeholder

```tsx
<Textarea placeholder="Tell us about your project" />
```

### With label and helper text

Labelled textarea with a hint

```tsx
<div className="space-y-1">
  <Label htmlFor="bio">Bio</Label>
  <Textarea id="bio" maxLength={280} />
  <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Up to 280 characters</p>
</div>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't use Textarea for single-line values** — Use Input for emails, names, and other short single-line data.
- **Don't use Textarea for rich text** — Textarea is plain text. Use a rich-text editor when formatting is required.

## Accessibility

- **Native semantics**: Wraps textarea; multiline text entry and form validation work natively
- **Character limits**: maxLength is supported natively

## Composition

- Compose with **Label** — Pair with Label for accessibility
  
  ```tsx
  <Label htmlFor="m">Message</Label><Textarea id="m" />
  ```
- Related: Input, Label

---

# ThemeToggle

Presentational light/dark toggle with accessible labels and sun/moon state.

> Import: `import { ThemeToggle } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/theme-toggle.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Theme persistence is app-specific (cookie, localStorage, server session), but the control is the same everywhere. ThemeToggle owns the button, icon state, and accessible label while the consumer owns storage and the actual class/attribute switch.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| theme | `'light' | 'dark'` | — | yes | Current theme. |
| onThemeChange | `(theme: 'light' | 'dark') => void` | — | yes | Fired with the next theme when the user toggles. |
| labels | `{ toLight?: string; toDark?: string }` | — | no | Accessible labels for the action that will happen next. |
| size | `'sm' | 'md'` | `md` | no | Control size. |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply. |

## Examples

### Cookie-backed theme

The consumer persists the theme; the component only renders and reports the next value.

```tsx
const [theme, setTheme] = useState<'light' | 'dark'>('light')

function change(next: 'light' | 'dark') {
  setTheme(next)
  document.documentElement.dataset.theme = next
  document.cookie = `theme=${next}; path=/; max-age=31536000`
}

<ThemeToggle theme={theme} onThemeChange={change} />
```

### Custom labels

```tsx
<ThemeToggle theme={theme} onThemeChange={setTheme} labels={{ toDark: 'Dark mode', toLight: 'Light mode' }} />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't let the component own persistence** — Theme storage differs by app (cookie for SSR, localStorage for SPAs). Keep persistence in the consumer and pass theme/onThemeChange.
- **Don't use an icon-only button without a label** — The component always sets aria-label and title; don't override them with empty values.

## Accessibility

- **Accessible name**: aria-label and title describe the next action, not the current state.
- **Keyboard**: Native button, Enter/Space activation, visible focus ring.
- **Icon semantics**: Icons are aria-hidden; the button label carries the meaning.

## Composition

- Compose with **SiteHeader** — Place in SiteHeader actions or the app shell header.
- Related: Button, SiteHeader, AppShell

---

# TimePicker

Native time field with an HH:MM contract and an optional clear button.

> Import: `import { TimePicker } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/time-picker.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Like DatePicker: the platform time control is already accessible and locale-aware. TimePicker standardizes the HH:MM contract and clear affordance.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| value | `string` | — | no | "HH:MM" (24h), controlled. |
| defaultValue | `string` | — | no | "HH:MM", initial value. |
| onValueChange | `(value: string) => void` | — | no | Fired with the time string; '' when cleared. |
| clearable | `boolean` | `false` | no | Shows a clear button once a value exists. |

## Examples

### Time field

Controlled HH:MM value.

```tsx
<TimePicker aria-label="Starts at" value={start} onValueChange={setStart} clearable />
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't mix 12h display with 24h state** — State stays HH:MM; format for display with Intl.

## Accessibility

- **Platform input**: Renders input[type=time]

## Composition

- Compose with **DatePicker** — Pair for date+time scheduling
  
  ```tsx
  <DatePicker aria-label="Date" /><TimePicker aria-label="Time" />
  ```
- Related: DatePicker, FormField, Input

# Timeline

Vertical chronology for experience, activity and audit trails, built on an ordered list.

> Import: `import { Timeline } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/timeline.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Chronologies communicate order. Rendering them as an ordered list keeps the sequence structural for assistive tech, while the connector rule and dots provide the visual rhythm.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| items | `{ title: string; period?: string; description?: string; icon?: ReactNode; muted?: boolean }[]` | — | yes | Ordered timeline entries. |

## Examples

### Experience

Period label, title and supporting line per entry.

```tsx
<Timeline
  items={[
    { title: 'Senior Engineer', period: '2023 — Present', description: 'Platform team' },
    { title: 'Engineer', period: '2020 — 2023' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't reverse the DOM order for newest-first** — Reverse the array instead so reading order matches visual order.

## Accessibility

- **Sequence**: Ordered list semantics

## Composition

- Compose with **Card** — Often embedded in profile/about cards
  
  ```tsx
  <Card><CardContent><Timeline items={roles} /></CardContent></Card>
  ```
- Related: List, Card, Separator

# Toast

Accessible notifications: tree-scoped provider/hook plus an imperative toast() API rendered by <Toaster />.

> Import: `import { ToastProvider } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/toast.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Toasts announce status changes without stealing focus. The provider/useToast pair covers tree-scoped usage; the module-level toast() + <Toaster /> covers event handlers and data layers where threading a hook is impossible (e.g. 1000+ call sites). A polite live region and auto-dismiss keep the queue quiet.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| title | `string` | — | yes | Toast heading. |
| description | `string` | — | no | Supporting line under the title. |
| variant | `'default' | 'success' | 'error' | 'warning' | 'info'` | `default` | no | Status accent (dot + optional rich tint). |
| action | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` | — | no | Single inline action; dismisses the toast after running. |
| duration | `number` | `5000` | no | Auto-dismiss delay in ms; 0 keeps the toast until dismissed. |
| position | `'top-left' | 'top-center' | 'top-right' | 'bottom-left' | 'bottom-center' | 'bottom-right'` | `bottom-right` | no | Toaster placement (Toaster component). |
| richColors | `boolean` | `false` | no | Tint the toast surface with its status color (Toaster component). |
| label | `string` | `Notifications` | no | Accessible name of the live region (Toaster component). |

## Examples

### Imperative API

Fire from event handlers or data layers — no hook needed.

```tsx
import { Toaster, toast } from '@slipstream-ui/core';

<Toaster position="bottom-right" richColors />

toast.success('Saved', 'Your changes are live');
toast.error('Upload failed', 'Check your connection');
toast({ title: 'Heads up', duration: 0 });
```

### Tree-scoped provider

Existing provider/hook pair for component-scoped usage.

```tsx
<ToastProvider>
  <App />
</ToastProvider>;

const { toast, dismiss } = useToast();
toast({ title: 'Saved' });
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not use toasts for critical errors** — Auto-dismissed messages can be missed. Render persistent inline error states (role=alert) for failures the user must resolve.

## Accessibility

- **Polite live region**: Each toast renders role=status inside a labelled list; announcements never steal focus
- **Dismiss control**: Every toast has a labelled dismiss button (Dismiss <title>)
- **Auto-dismiss timing**: 5s default; duration 0 keeps sticky toasts

## Composition

- Compose with **Toaster** — Mount once near the app root next to your router; keep it outside transforms so fixed positioning is not affected
  
  ```tsx
  <App><Toaster /></App>
  ```
- Compose with **ToastProvider** — Use the provider/hook pair when the call site is inside the React tree
  
  ```tsx
  <ToastProvider><App /></ToastProvider>
  ```
- Related: Confirmation, Button

---

# ToolCall

A component for displaying AI tool/function calls with status, arguments, and results

> Import: `import { ToolCall } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/tool-call.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/ai

## Design intent

The ToolCall component visualizes when an AI agent uses tools or functions. It shows the tool name, status (pending, running, completed, failed), arguments passed, and the result returned. This provides transparency into the AI's actions.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| toolCall | `ToolCall` | — | yes | The tool call object containing name, arguments, status, and result |
| showResult | `boolean` | `true` | no | Whether to display the tool result |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |
| labels | `{ pending?: string; running?: string; completed?: string; failed?: string; arguments?: string; result?: string; error?: string }` | — | no | Localized status and section labels. |

## Examples

### Completed tool call

Tool call that completed successfully with result

```tsx
<ToolCall 
  toolCall={{
    id: '1',
    name: 'search',
    arguments: { query: 'React components' },
    status: 'completed',
    result: { results: [...] }
  }}
/>
```

### Running tool call

Tool call currently in progress

```tsx
<ToolCall 
  toolCall={{
    id: '2',
    name: 'calculate',
    arguments: { expression: '2 + 2' },
    status: 'running'
  }}
/>
```

### Failed tool call

Tool call that failed with error message

```tsx
<ToolCall 
  toolCall={{
    id: '3',
    name: 'api_request',
    arguments: { endpoint: '/users' },
    status: 'failed',
    result: { error: 'Timeout' }
  }}
/>
```

### Without result

Tool call with result hidden

```tsx
<ToolCall 
  toolCall={toolCall}
  showResult={false}
/>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't show tool calls for simple operations** — Tool calls should be shown for meaningful operations, not trivial ones.
- **Don't expose sensitive data in arguments** — Never display sensitive credentials or personal data in tool call arguments.
- **Don't ignore failed tool calls** — Failed tool calls should be clearly indicated with error information.

## Accessibility

- **Status indication**: Status is shown with both color and text label for clarity
- **Code readability**: Arguments and results are displayed in pre/code blocks with proper formatting
- **Structure**: Tool call information is organized in clear sections (header, arguments, result)

## Composition

- Compose with **Message** — ToolCall components are typically displayed within assistant messages to show tool usage
  
  ```tsx
  Message component can contain ToolCall to show when the AI used tools during its response
  ```
- Compose with **Reasoning** — Reasoning often precedes ToolCall to explain why a tool is being invoked
  
  ```tsx
  Reasoning explains the decision to use a tool, ToolCall shows the actual invocation
  ```
- Related: Message, Reasoning, Conversation

---

# Tooltip

Hover/focus tooltip with aria-describedby association, delay, and Escape dismissal

> Import: `import { Tooltip } from '@slipstream-ui/core'`
> Registry: https://slipstreamui.com/registry/tooltip.json
> Tier: molecule · Package: @slipstream-ui/core

## Design intent

Tooltip provides supplementary context on hover and keyboard focus. It appears with a short delay, is announced via aria-describedby, and dismisses on Escape so it never traps the user.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| content | `string` | — | yes | The tooltip text |
| side | `'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right'` | `top` | no | Placement relative to the trigger |
| delay | `number` | `300` | no | Delay before showing on hover, in milliseconds |
| children | `ReactNode` | — | yes | The trigger element |
| className | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Examples

### Button with tooltip

Supplementary hint on a button

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Save your changes">
  <Button>Save</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

### Custom placement

Tooltip placed to the right with a short delay

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Opens in a new tab" side="right" delay={100}>
  <a href="/docs">Docs</a>
</Tooltip>
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't put essential information only in a tooltip** — Tooltips are unavailable on touch devices and to keyboard users in some contexts. Required information must be visible in the UI.
- **Don't use tooltips for interactive content** — Tooltip content is not focusable; use a Popover for links or buttons inside the hint.

## Accessibility

- **aria-describedby association**: The tooltip id is linked to the trigger when visible
- **Keyboard focus support**: Shows on focus as well as hover
- **Escape dismissal**: Escape hides the tooltip without moving focus

## Composition

- Compose with **Button / IconButton** — Wrap icon-only buttons with a Tooltip to name them
  
  ```tsx
  <Tooltip content="Close"><Button aria-label="Close">×</Button></Tooltip>
  ```
- Related: Button, Label
